title: Director of Client Experience
description:
The Director of Client Experience sets the strategy for client engagement and service delivery across the third-party administration (TPA) portfolio. This role builds trusted partnerships with clients, brokers, carriers, and internal executives; translates client priorities into coordinated action; and holds teams accountable for delivering measurable results. The Director leads retention, renewals, implementations, executive reporting, and continuous improvement while identifying opportunities to strengthen partnerships and expand revenue. Success requires executive presence, sound knowledge of claims and TPA operations, disciplined execution, and the ability to influence outcomes across complex, cross-functional environments.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Support and lead a high-performing Client Experience team, setting clear expectations, developing talent, and fostering accountability for client and business outcomes.
  • Serve as the relationship leader for clients, brokers, consultants, carriers, vendors, and other stakeholders, aligning expectations, contractual commitments, and program priorities.
  • Own end-to-end client service delivery for TPA claims programs, including account management, issue resolution, reporting, contract administration, renewals, implementations, and ongoing communication.
  • Manage contract administration and renewal activities, including contract profiles, key dates, pricing changes, required approvals, authorized signatures, and coordination with finance, legal, compliance, and leadership.
  • Own the development, approval, maintenance, and distribution of client-specific service instructions, including contacts, authority levels, reporting schedules, service standards, escalation protocols, and special handling requirements.
  • Act as the senior escalation point for complex client concerns, service issues, claim handling inquiries, compliance-related matters, and operational challenges.
  • Partner with claims operations to monitor claim performance, claim quality, closing ratios, reserves, litigation trends, turnaround times, diary compliance, responsiveness, and adherence to service level agreements.
  • Coordinate with carriers, excess insurers, medical management vendors, bill review providers, legal partners, loss control resources, and technology vendors to support client program objectives.
  • Develop and implement standardized TPA client service procedures, workflows, communication standards, claim review protocols, stewardship processes, and escalation practices.
  • Analyze client feedback, claim trends, loss data, service metrics, and performance reports to identify improvement opportunities and recommend practical solutions.
  • Shape retention and growth strategy in partnership with sales, business development, and executive leadership; to support, qualify opportunities, strengthen proposals and prepare RFP and RFI responses, contribute to pricing strategy, identify organic growth and cross-selling opportunities within existing client and broker relationships.
  • Lead full cycle onboarding and implementation of new TPA clients, including service calendars, trust-account or prefunding coordination, invoicing setup, data conversion, system configuration, client access, reporting, coding, regulatory reporting setup, staffing assignments, kickoff meetings, operational readiness, and post-implementation follow-up.
  • Coordinate client technology and reporting needs, including claims-system access and training, custom reports, scheduled reporting, data feeds, conversions, reconciliations, and data-quality validation.
  • Establish account service calendars and governance routines; document decisions, owners, and deadlines; monitor aging items and service commitments; and escalate missed deliverables or unresolved risks.
  • Coordinate staffing transitions that affect clients, including communication plans, required client approvals, candidate qualifications and interviews, interim coverage, and continuity of service.
  • Partner with finance and operations on trust accounts, prefunding, invoicing, fee schedules, contract pricing, payment reporting, and resolution of related client financial inquiries.
  • Coordinate client, carrier, broker, and internal audits; track corrective actions; and confirm that reporting, compliance, and claim-handling commitments are completed.
  • Prepare and deliver client business reviews, claim review materials, stewardship reports, performance dashboards, renewal support summaries, and executive presentations.
  • Ensure client service practices align with applicable laws, insurance regulations, contractual requirements, privacy obligations, carrier guidelines, and internal TPA policies.
  • Operate within, and escalate, technical claim issues while respecting delegated authority and established; do not independently direct claim outcomes, waive defenses, provide legal, regulatory, and claim-handling protocols, directing appropriate escalation of matters that require technical, legal advice, or exercise settlement authority unless expressly authorized.
  • Set departmental priorities and direct staffing, resources, performance standards, service commitments, budget stewardship responsibilities, and client satisfaction objectives to achieve portfolio and organizational goals, as assigned.
  • Establish performance standards and metrics for team members, including client satisfaction, renewals, new client onboarding, client change requests, implementations, escalations handling and resolution, reporting accuracy, service-level compliance; intervene decisively when results fall below expectations with corrective actions.
  • Champion a culture of ownership, responsiveness, professional judgment, claims advocacy, and continuous improvement.

Measurable Success Metrics

  • Maintain annual client retention at or above 95%, excluding planned exits or accounts outside the role’s control.
  • Achieve an average client satisfaction score of at least 4.5 out of 5, or an equivalent established benchmark, with documented action plans for scores below target.
  • Complete at least 95% of renewals, contract amendments, and required approvals by the established due date.
  • Deliver at least 90% of new-client implementations by the agreed launch date, with no material unresolved operational, financial, reporting, or system issues at go-live.
  • Acknowledge urgent client escalations within one business day and resolve or establish a documented action plan for at least 90% within five business days.
  • Deliver at least 98% of scheduled client reports, stewardship materials, and business-review deliverables accurately and on time.
  • Maintain at least 95% compliance with contractual service levels, client-specific instructions, reporting schedules, and documented follow-up commitments.
  • Close at least 90% of audit findings and corrective actions by the agreed deadline, with no repeat material findings attributable to client service oversight.
  • Maintain complete and current client profiles, service instructions, contract records, and account calendars for 100% of assigned accounts, reviewed at least annually and after material changes.
  • Identify, document, and advance qualified retention, cross-selling, or organic growth opportunities in alignment with annual revenue goals established by leadership.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Risk Management, Insurance, Healthcare Administration, Human Resources, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered.
  • Minimum of 8 years of progressive experience in client services, account management, claims administration, third-party administration, insurance brokerage, carrier operations, risk management, or a related service environment.
  • Minimum of 3 years of leadership experience managing client-facing teams in a TPA, claims, insurance, or risk management setting.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex employer, broker, carrier, or consultant relationships and resolving escalated service or claims-related issues.
  • Deep understanding of TPA operations, claims administration, contractual service levels, executive reporting, stewardship, claim review practices, compliance expectations, and client communication standards.
  • Working knowledge of one or more claims lines, such as workers’ compensation, general liability, property, auto, disability, leave administration, or employee benefits.
  • Excellent verbal, written, presentation, and executive communication skills, including the ability to explain claims and service issues clearly to clients and internal stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to analyze loss data, claim trends, service metrics, and operational performance to develop practical recommendations.
  • Strong organizational, problem-solving, project management, and cross-functional leadership skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and experience using claims management, RMIS, CRM, or client service platforms.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working for a third-party administrator, claims management organization, insurance brokerage, carrier, self-insured employer program, or risk management services firm.
  • Experience supporting self-insured, high-deductible, loss-sensitive, or administratively serviced insurance programs.
  • Experience supporting municipalities, public agencies, or other public-sector entities, including public contracting, statutory claim requirements, governing board or council processes, and coordination with public counsel.
  • Knowledge of workers’ compensation, general liability, auto liability, property, professional liability, disability, leave administration, employee benefits, or other applicable claims lines.
  • Experience leading claim reviews, client stewardship meetings, quarterly business reviews, renewal strategy meetings, or executive-level client presentations.
  • Professional designation or certification related to claims, insurance, risk management, benefits, or project management is a plus, such as ARM, AIC, CPCU, WCP, SHRM, CEBS, or PMP.

Key Competencies

  • TPA client relationship management and executive presence
  • Claims advocacy and operational service orientation
  • Leadership, coaching, and team development
  • Claims administration knowledge and sound technical judgment
  • Service excellence, client retention, and renewal support
  • Strategic thinking, workflow design, and process improvement
  • Problem-solving, negotiation, and conflict resolution
  • Data-driven claims and service performance management
  • Executive influence and cross-functional leadership across claims, sales, compliance, finance, technology, carriers, brokers, and vendors
  • Decisive prioritization and disciplined execution in a fast-paced, client-focused TPA environment

Work Environment and Expectations

  • Travel as needed to strengthen client partnerships, lead stewardship and executive presentations, support industry engagement, and align internal teams.
  • Exercise sound judgment and discretion in managing sensitive client, financial, contractual, and claims-related information.
  • Provide leadership outside standard business hours when significant client or operational matters require timely executive attention.

title: Neuropsychologist
description:
The Clinical Neuropsychologist, with NYS Psychology license, will provide comprehensive Neuropsychological assessment and related clinical services across New York locations, including Long Island, NYC/Brooklyn, and Westchester (Yonkers or New Rochelle), and support as needed to Northern New Jersey location (Fairfield) and as licensure allows.


The role requires formal education (PhD or PsyD) and clinical training, clinical internship and post-doctoral training in Neuropsychology, and experience in Neuropsychological assessment (and cognitive remediation services preferred), including clinical interviewing, test selection and interpretation, diagnostic formulation, comprehensive report writing, and treatment plan development.


The Neuropsychologist role requires specialization in diagnosing, treating, and managing disorders affecting the brain/central nervous system. The role requires experience working with adult patients, although experience across the lifespan (5+ to geriatric patients) is a plus. Experience is required with neurodegenerative conditions (e.g., Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease), traumatic brain injury, strokes, seizure disorders, and other medical, neurological, psychiatric, and neurodevelopmental conditions.


The Clinical Neuropsychologist will manage assigned evaluations, participate in clinical consultation and case review, and collaborate with the multidisciplinary clinical team. The Neuropsychologist will consult with members of a multi-disciplinary clinical team as well as external referral sources to ensure the appropriate course of treatment. The Clinical Neuropsychologist will also supervise and lead/co-lead cognitive remediation group sessions for patients with cognitive impairment stemming from psychiatric, neurological, medical, and neurodevelopmental conditions.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Conduct comprehensive Neuropsychological evaluations under the direction of the Chief of Neuropsychology to assess cognitive, emotional, behavioral, and psychological functioning in individuals with conditions such as traumatic brain injury (TBI), stroke, dementia, ADHD, learning disorders, and other neurological, medical, psychiatric, or neurodevelopmental conditions.
  • Complete clinical interviews, review relevant medical and clinical records, select appropriate assessment measures, interpret test results, and integrate findings into comprehensive Neuropsychological reports.
  • Develop clinically appropriate diagnostic impressions, recommendations, and individualized treatment or rehabilitation plans based on exam findings and patient needs.
  • Provide evidence-based therapeutic interventions, as appropriate within scope of evaluation and cognitive remediation treatment, including cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), mindfulness-based strategies, and trauma-focused approaches to support patients experiencing anxiety, depression, PTSD, psychosocial adjustment difficulties, and other concerns related to Neurological, medical, psychiatric, or neurodevelopmental conditions.
  • Participate in clinical consultation and case review with the Chief of Neuropsychology, including discussion of complex cases, diagnostic considerations, and treatment recommendations.
  • Provide clinical services for injured workers (workers’ compensation) and patients injured in motor vehicle accident (no-fault) cases when applicable, including Neuropsychological evaluation, treatment recommendations, and coordination with appropriate clinical and rehabilitation resources.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, when clinically appropriate, to coordinate comprehensive care and support return-to-function or return-to-work goals.
  • Provide services across designated New York locations, including Long Island, NYC/Brooklyn, and Westchester, with Northern New Jersey coverage as needed and as licensure allows.
  • Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation, including Neuropsychological evaluation reports, treatment progress notes and treatment plans, in accordance with professional, regulatory, and organizational standards.
  • Support the continued growth and development of PAX Health’s Neuropsychology Division.
  • Abide by PAX Health ethics and model values.
  • Other clinical and administrative duties as needed within the scope of the role.

title: Information Security & IT Manager

As a hands-on Information Security & IT Manager, you’d manage the day-to-day security and IT operations. You’d work closely with LawY’s Engineering, Product and business teams to maintain a secure, reliable and well-managed technology environment. You will also work with CORTO Information Security, which will provide broader governance, standards and oversight.

This is a broad role suited to someone comfortable working across information security, IT operations, cloud security, compliance and risk management.

LawY operates in a modern cloud and AI-enabled environment. Its production platform is hosted with a major cloud provider and uses AI models and services to process information, while its developers use approved AI-assisted development platforms as part of their daily workflows.

To make this happen you will:

  • Manage day-to-day information security and IT operations for LawY.
  • Maintain security controls across cloud, applications, endpoints, identity and SaaS platforms.
  • Monitor and respond to security alerts, incidents and vulnerabilities.
  • Coordinate remediation activities with Engineering, Product and third-party providers.
  • Manage user access, onboarding, offboarding, devices and endpoint security.
  • Administer identity and access management and Microsoft 365, including Entra ID, Exchange Online, SharePoint, Defender for Business and relevant security controls.
  • Manage User devices through MDM platforms.
  • Support and manage enterprise applications, SaaS platforms, licensing, integrations and technology vendors.
  • Maintain LawY’s network infrastructure and coordinate troubleshooting or improvements with internal teams and specialist providers.
  • Support secure software development, architecture reviews and penetration testing.
  • Maintain security documentation, risk registers, procedures and asset inventories.
  • Support SOC 2, privacy, audits, customer security reviews and compliance activities.
  • Manage security and technology vendors.
  • Provide regular reporting on security risks, incidents and remediation progress.
  • Escalate material risks and incidents to LawY leadership and CORTO Information Security.

What you’ll bring

You will have experience across information security, IT operations or cloud security within a technology or SaaS environment.

  • Experience with cloud security, identity and access management, endpoint security and vulnerability management.
  • Strong hands-on experience administering Microsoft 365, Entra ID, MDM and Microsoft security tools.
  • Experience managing enterprise applications, SaaS platforms and technology vendors.
  • A strong understanding of network architecture, connectivity and network security principles.
  • Experience supporting incident response and security monitoring.
  • A good understanding of secure software development and application security.
  • Experience supporting compliance frameworks such as SOC 2 or ISO 27001.
  • Familiarity with AWS, Vercel and modern cloud-based and AI-enabled technology environments.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • The ability to work independently in a practical, hands-on role.
  • A risk-based approach to solving security and technology challenges.

Even better if you have

  • Experience supporting SaaS businesses that use AI platforms in development or production.
  • Experience with SIEM, EDR, vulnerability management, GRC or cloud security tools.
  • Experience in legal technology, SaaS or another regulated environment.
  • Relevant Microsoft 365, endpoint administration, AWS or networking certifications would be advantageous.
  • Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CCSP, Security+, AWS Security Specialty or ISO 27001.

LawY is an inclusive, people-first company committed to breaking down institutional barriers that keep people from reaching their potential. If you meet some, but not all the requirements above, we encourage you to still submit your application.

Why join LawY?

  • Your work matters. We solve real world problems that improve and support local, everyday law firms. So they can do their best work for the people in the communities they serve.
  • Make an impact. You won’t be another ‘cog in the wheel’ here. We give full trust and autonomy for you to be heard, to work on big & complex projects – and to make a real difference.
  • Work with a group of authentic, passionate people who love what they do.
  • Genuine startup energy - small team, fast decisions, real trajectory, backed by one of the largest legal software companies in the world.
  • Flexible and hybrid working. We engage, share, and collaborate on ideas and workflows.
  • Career and learning opportunities - we move fast and need smart people to get us where we're going. We are a scaling business and looking for people who want to grow with us.
  • Have fun with us. Celebrations. Socials. Sports teams. Access to sailing and yacht events.

  • Fast-paced tech environment, if we don't disrupt ourselves someone else will do it!

title: Senior Data Scientist
description:
About Warden AI

Warden AI helps HR Tech vendors, staffing firms, and employers prove and improve the fairness, accuracy, and compliance of their AI hiring systems. In a fast-changing regulatory environment, organizations need a trusted partner to validate their AI, and Warden is quickly becoming the default solution.

In 2025, Warden grew from 4 to 40 customers. In 2026, we’ve already more than doubled ARR and are growing faster every quarter. That growth is driven not just by market demand, but by something rarer: a genuine network effect. Customers want to promote working with Warden because it helps them win their own deals.

About the role

We're hiring a Senior Data Scientist / Senior Applied Scientist to run highly defensible bias audits of high-stakes AI systems, used everywhere from startups to industry-leading enterprises. These audits carry real weight with regulators, courts, customers and candidates, and the methodology behind them has to hold up. The role spans AI system evaluation, rigorous statistical analysis, synthetic data generation, and an applied understanding of hiring and selection procedures.

You'll join a team with deep expertise in behavioral and social sciences, evaluation methodology, and structured bias testing. You'll need strong statistical and probabilistic reasoning: fluency with techniques like uncertainty quantification, experimental design, causal inference and Bayesian modeling. Just as essential is commercial instinct: the judgment to design rigorous, workable methods within real product goals and constraints, built through meaningful, hands-on experience shipping at startup speed.

You will report to the CTO and work closely with the founders and product team across hands-on analysis, methodological design, and strategic thinking. As one of a small number of data hires, you will have high agency to shape both how our analytical function evolves and the scope of your own role as we grow.

What you’ll do

Here are a few examples of things you might be working on:

  • Set and uphold rigorous statistical methodology. Define the statistical tests, fairness metrics, sampling strategies, and evaluation frameworks we rely on, and embed the checks and validation patterns that keep our analytical work accurate, reproducible, and defensible.
  • Translate regulations and standards into practical tests. Work with our policy experts to translate legal requirements, guidance, and emerging HR and AI standards into clear, practical audit methodologies.
  • Design the foundations for audit execution. Create the datasets, test frameworks, workflows, and analysis patterns that enable consistent, efficient, and high-quality audits, and help establish the data partnerships that inform our synthetic data generation and audit methodology.
  • Analyze and interpret audit results. Assess what results do and don't show given uncertainty and limitations, and shape how findings are presented to customers through our reports and dashboards, including actionable insight like pointing to the likely source when an audit fails.
  • Support key high-stakes conversations. Bring technical authority on data, methodology, and statistical defensibility to stakeholder discussions, including with customers' own data science, legal and compliance teams.
  • Document and defend our methodology. Write the accessible explanations, white papers and industry reports that let regulators, customers and outside experts scrutinize our approach and trust the results.

What you should bring

  • 5+ years in a commercial, high-performing product organization doing applied statistics or data science - not solely academic or research-lab experience.
  • Strong statistical and probabilistic reasoning, with hands-on fluency in confidence intervals and hypothesis testing, power analysis, experimental design, causal inference, and Bayesian modeling.
  • Experience designing evaluation methodologies - including black-box and counterfactual approaches - and the test datasets behind them, with good judgment on realism and validity limits.
  • Practical familiarity with evaluating AI systems and their failure modes, across classic ML models, LLM-based systems, and AI agents.
  • Fluency in Python for statistical analysis, data preparation, and reproducible evaluation workflows.
  • A rigorous approach that values evidence, clarity, and defensibility, producing analysis that stands up to scrutiny.
  • Comfort with open-ended problems and the ability to bring structure where none exists.
  • Clear, responsible communication, with the ability to adapt complex ideas for different audiences, and a collaborative, high-agency way of working with colleagues across the company and with customers.

Nice to have, not required:

  • Background in HR analytics / I/O psychology / Psychometrics (selection processes, adverse impact analysis, etc)
  • Familiarity with AI and hiring regulation, especially translating its requirements into testable criteria.
  • First-hand experience with how modern agentic AI systems are built and their behavior emerges
  • Experience with explainability for black-box systems (surrogate modeling, behavioral analysis, etc)

This role isn’t for you if…

  • You've only worked in academic or research settings and haven't applied statistics to real commercial product decisions.
  • You prefer narrow, well-scoped analytical problems over work that spans statistics, regulation, product, and customer context.
  • You need complete information before acting, rather than exercising judgment under uncertainty and evolving guidance.
  • You'd rather follow established methods than create structure from ambiguity; defining and refining our evaluation process is core to the job.
  • You're uncomfortable owning the quality bar and being the one who decides whether an analysis is defensible enough to publish.
  • You prefer to stay behind the scenes rather than join high-stakes customer conversations where clarity and statistical judgement matter.
  • You'd rather avoid external scrutiny of your work; ours is shared with enterprise stakeholders and the wider ecosystem, including in public-facing materials.

What we offer:

  • £100-120k+ base salary + meaningful equity in a rapidly growing business
  • Private health insurance
  • 33 days holiday (incl. bank holidays)
  • Hybrid working model (3 days/week in our London office)
  • Learning and Development budget of £500 per year

Interview process

Our interview process involves the following stages:

  1. Initial screen (30min) - Intro call to align on your background and the role.
  2. Founder screen (40min + 40min) - CEO: how you act, decide, and adapt, and how that translates into a high-agency, fast-moving startup environment. CTO: your fit against the role's requirements, from statistical rigor to product instinct.
  3. Take-home task - Short analytical case study, designed for 2-3 hours, drawn from the challenges we face; it sets up the on-site case review.
  4. On-site interview (50min + 50min) - A collaborative case review, and an evaluation scenario, reasoning through its design and uncertainties.
  5. Reference checks & Offer - We move quickly from references to a clear offer.

If you have any specific questions or want to talk through reasonable adjustments ahead of or during the application, please contact us at any point at hiring@warden-ai.com.

Equal opportunities for everyone

Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us, and we are making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Warden AI. We embrace diversity in all of its forms and create an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of supporting the responsible adoption of AI systems.

We’re an equal-opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, veteran status, neurodiversity status or disability status.

title: Senior Hardware Reliability & Test Engineer
description:
Who we are

Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.

Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.

Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.

This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.

We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.

If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.

About the role

Atoms is seeking a Senior Hardware Reliability & Environmental Test Engineer to set the hardware qualification standard and own reliability and environmental testing across our platforms. The role covers the qualification standard itself, reliability requirements and budgets, the design verification plan, environmental and accelerated life testing, and analysis that turns test and field data into design and test changes.

What you’ll do

  • Define hardware qualification standards, including environmental requirements, test methods, and acceptance criteria.
  • Define reliability and availability requirements for hardware systems and subsystems.
  • Own the design verification plan and report, covering thermal cycling, shock, humidity, vibration, dust and water ingress, corrosion, altitude and fluid resistance.
  • Collect and analyze field load data, and derive mission profiles and accelerated test profiles from measured operating conditions.
  • Own the environmental test equipment plan and its justification. Specify, commission and maintain equipment, fixturing, instrumentation and calibration records, and determine which testing runs internally and which is run with external labs.
  • Own external test lab relationships.
  • Plan and execute HALT for design margin and accelerated life testing for life estimation.
  • Lead DFMEA, fault tree analysis and reliability block diagram activities and track the resulting actions into the verification plan.
  • Analyze field failures and returned hardware, drive root cause and corrective action, and revise test requirements based on the results.
  • Set the reliability acceptance criteria suppliers are held to, review and challenge supplier qualification data, and specify additional testing where application conditions are not covered.

What we’re looking for

  • Bachelor's degree in mechanical, electrical, materials or a related engineering field. Equivalent hands-on experience will be considered in place of the degree.
  • Deployed fleet experience in autonomous vehicles, EV, or robotics.
  • 10+ years in hardware reliability, environmental test or design validation on electromechanical and electronic hardware.
  • Ownership of environmental and accelerated life test programs end to end across multiple products or programs, including test plan development, level and duration selection, execution and reporting.
  • Experience defining a reliability or qualification standard applied by more than one team, and driving adoption across teams outside your reporting line.
  • Working knowledge of test methods, with the ability to tailor test requirements to an application.
  • Experience deriving test profiles from measured field data, including instrumentation, data acquisition and post-processing.
  • Proficiency in DFMEA, fault tree analysis, reliability block diagrams, reliability growth and Weibull analysis.
  • Ability to work onsite five days a week in San Francisco, with travel to production and field sites.

Why join us

At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.

What else you need to know

This role is based in our San Francisco office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.

The base salary range for this role is $182,000 - $238,000 per year.

Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package. You may also be eligible for equity awards.

Benefits Summary (USA Full-Time Exempt Employees):

  • Medical, Dental, Vision, Disability, and Life Insurance
  • Flexible Spending Account / Health Savings Account Options

  • Equity
  • Sick Time, Unlimited Flexible Time Off, and Paid Holidays
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Pre-Tax Commuter Benefit Plan
  • Team lunch in our SoMa office every Tuesday and Thursday

Benefits are subject to change at the company's discretion.
Atoms accepts applications on an ongoing basis.

Ready to join us as we serve those who serve others?

title: YCBA Museum Photographer
description:
Working at Yale means contributing to a better tomorrow. Whether you are a current resident of our New Haven-based community, eligible for opportunities through the New Haven Hiring Initiative, or a newcomer, interested in exploring all that Yale has to offer, your talents and contributions are welcome. Discover your opportunities at Yale!

Overview

Reporting to the Head of Imaging and Intellectual Property, the Museum Photographer creates high-quality images of museum, library, and archive collections at the Yale Center for British Art (YCBA). The photographer also undertakes photo and video documentation of YCBA facilities, exhibitions, programs, and events for archival and promotional use.

The photographer works both independently and as a member of a team of department photographers and technicians to meet imaging objectives. The photographer fulfills routine work orders according to established procedures. The photographer also evaluates and carries out projects, consulting with staff to develop an understanding of aesthetic, technical, logistical, and scheduling requirements.

The photographer transports objects to and from studios independently or with the assistance of collections staff when appropriate. They verify object identification, handle objects on set, and practice safe lighting and support methods according to museum conservation protocols. They ensure security of objects from pickup or arrival in the studio until release.

The photographer captures, evaluates, and adjusts digital image files for quality and accuracy, including exposure, gray and color balance, sharpness, contrast, and density. They maintain color management standards and workflows, creating custom ICC color profiles for a variety of capture settings and regularly monitoring settings for software and hardware used to capture, edit, and view images. They undertake post-processing of digital image files, including verification of objects or subjects photographed; file naming; applying technical or administrative metadata; editing or versioning digital files manually or using actions/scripts, including rotation, straightening, cropping, and appending digital color bars; checking files against work orders; and verifying transfer of image files from capture workstation to servers.



Required Skills and Abilities

Excellent written/verbal communication skills. Demonstrated ability to work both independently and in a team, meet deadlines, and adapt to change. Track record of diligent performance, reliability, accuracy, and attention to detail, supported by references. Ability to document 2D and 3D collection objects using a variety of still and analytical photography techniques, including but not limited to visible light photography, reflected and transmitted infrared photography, and ultraviolet photography. Demonstrated ability to meet established cultural heritage digitization guidelines in production. Ability to discern subtle variation in tone and color and to adjust digital images and print output to match target values and originals. Comprehensive understanding of digital image file parameters. Demonstrated command of photographic equipment and systems, including medium-format digital, DSLR, and modified cameras; strobe and continuous lighting; filters; and diffusers. Ability to troubleshoot equipment, hardware, and software, and to solve routine as well as novel technical issues. Excellent computer skills. Expert skill with industry-standard tools and systems to capture, edit and print digital images. Proficiency with MacOS; familiarity with Windows OS and Microsoft 365. Keeps current with technological developments and innovations in cultural heritage digitization.


Preferred Skills and Abilities

Principal Responsibilities

1. Views subjects and settings and plans compositions, camera positions, and camera angles to produce desired effects. 2. Evaluates the technical requirements of complex projects. Determines the most appropriate techniques and methods as well as time needed to complete assignments or projects. (Assignments may require innovation to resolve problems that are not necessarily governed by established procedures.) 3. Selects and assembles equipment according to subject material, anticipated conditions, and knowledge of function of various types of cameras, lenses, films, and accessories. 4. Provides color management support; matches hues and tones of digital files to original objects. 5. Maintains and monitors condition of equipment and software used to capture, edit and view images. 6. May perform other duties as assigned. Required Education and Experience Bachelor’s Degree in a related field and two years of related work experience in the same job family; or an equivalent combination of education and related experience.

title: Principal AMO Physicist
description:
Contract Type: Full-time, Permanent

Location: Cambridge, UK

Visa Sponsorship available

Join Nu Quantum - Shaping the Future of Technology

Nu Quantum is at the forefront of quantum computing and advanced technology, driven by innovation, diversity, and a commitment to excellence. We’re creating an environment where brilliant minds from all backgrounds collaborate to push the boundaries of what’s possible.

Founded to commercialise research generated over the last decade at the Cavendish Laboratory, Nu Quantum is on a mission to shape the future of quantum information systems.

We’re working on exciting technology that will improve the utility and accelerate the time-to-market of quantum computing systems. We integrate novel quantum photonic technology to form an efficient and scalable quantum networking infrastructure in partnership with world-leading companies and academic groups.

About the role
We’re looking for a skilled and experienced experimental Physicist, to join our trapped-ion testbed. Our AMO team are currently interfacing our integrated microcavity-technology with trapped-ion qubits and benchmarking the efficiency of the ion-photon interface, and the fidelity of remote entanglement between trapped-ion nodes. This quantum-network demonstrator is a cornerstone of Nu Quantum’s mission to create scalable, high-performance quantum networks.

In this role, you’ll work at the intersection of atomic physics, cavity QED, and quantum engineering, joining the AMO physics team and collaborating closely with experts across electronics, optics, and mechanical design. You’ll play a key role in demonstrating Nu Quantum’s proprietary qubit–photon interface technology, helping us push toward state-of-the-art entanglement rates and fidelities.

This is a highly cross-functional, hands-on role where creative problem-solving and system-level thinking are essential. You’ll have the opportunity to shape next-generation designs, drive technical innovation, and directly contribute to the long-term vision of making quantum networking a reality.

If you’re excited by the challenge of interconnecting quantum computers — and want to work on technology that’s defining the field — we’d love to hear from you.

What you'll be doing

  • Design and execute remote-entanglement experiments to benchmark and advance ion-trapping devices with Nu Quantum’s integrated micro-cavity technology.
  • Mentor and support AMO Physicists, helping them grow technical depth, independence, and problem-solving capability.
  • Develop, maintain, and troubleshoot laboratory systems — including laser setups, RF/DC electronics, control systems, and ultra-high-vacuum hardware.
  • Collaborate across disciplines with Software, Optical, Mechanical, and Electrical Engineers, as well as with theory and simulation teams, to deliver integrated experimental systems.
  • Keep project teams and Project Management Office aligned through clear, timely communication of results, progress, and priorities across interdependent, fast-moving workstreams.
  • Establish and uphold best practices in laboratory safety, documentation, and system reliability.
  • Contribute to technical strategy, identifying opportunities to improve experimental design, automation, and scalability.

Requirements

We’re looking for someone who has:

Leadership experience

  • Past experience providing technical leadership within a collaborative team to deliver complex projects in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proven track record of managing research grants or leading multidisciplinary projects in industry.
  • A proven track record in scientific communication (papers, talks, conferences).

Expertise

  • Experience in experimental AMO physics, preferably in ion-trapping, or a related discipline.
  • Hands-on experience with quantum control of qubits with optical fields, gate optimisation and benchmarking.
  • Deep understanding of qubit control, atomic physics and atom–phonon interactions.

Skills

  • Expertise in at least two of these areas: sub-kHz laser locking, system automation, and real-time control (e.g. ARTIQ).
  • A system-level mindset — comfortable defining requirements and connecting hardware, software, and control layers.
  • Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the confidence to take initiative, make independent technical decisions, and drive solutions forward.
  • Willingness to mentor others and a readiness to take ownership of technical direction as the team grows.

Benefits

Why Work with Us?

At Nu Quantum, we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where people of all identities, orientations, backgrounds, and experiences are empowered. We value diverse perspectives as a source of creativity and innovation and encourage applications from all backgrounds, including those from underrepresented and marginalised communities. Joining Nu Quantum means joining a team where you can grow professionally and be part of an inspiring mission to shape the future of technology.

Benefits

  • Flexible working options
  • 28 days annual leave, inclusive of a 3-day company shutdown period + UK Bank Holidays
  • Option to purchase up to 5 days holiday per year

  • Enhanced paid family leave policies

Job Summary:

This position is focused on clinical and translational cancer research rather than basic science laboratory research. While the position supports research studies and clinical trials, it does not involve bench science, laboratory experimentation, or routine operation of scientific laboratory equipment. Training in mixed methods techniques as applied to clinical trial recruitment will be provided. The successful candidate will work closely with multidisciplinary research teams, patients, and study sites to support recruitment, implementation, and development of clinical research studies.

In 1930, Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery (Oto-HNS) was added as a division within the University of Wisconsin Department of Surgery. In 2025, after decades of growth and achievement, the division became an independent department within the School of Medicine and Public Health. Oto-HNS includes seven divisions: otology and neurotology, laryngology, pediatric otolaryngology, comprehensive otolaryngology, rhinology and skull base surgery, head and neck oncologic surgery, and facial plastic and reconstructive surgery. We provide a full range of state-of-the-art specialized care for adults and children at six clinical practice sites in the Madison area, and six outreach sites across Wisconsin and Illinois. Our team of nationally and internationally renowned faculty and residents prioritizes a collaborative culture, engaging with specialists across our practice sites and throughout campus. The department offers the highest quality of education to a large variety of learners, providing training to well over 100 individuals each year through clinical rotations, extramurally funded traineeships, externships and more.

The successful candidate will have knowledge of library technical services and demonstrate the ability to take initiative and work collaboratively.

Job Description

The Information Specialist is an individual contributor role that supports Par Health’s Generics (Gx) and Sterile Injectable (SI) businesses with potential to support all sites and all departments while primarily supporting R&D, Regulatory, Pharmacovigilance, and Quality.

Key Accountabilities

Company

  • Database Management (i.e., Ovid, Accuris, USP, EP, BP, Scifinder, etc)

Company

  • Iron Mountain Administrator

Regulatory

  • Supports Regulatory Annual Reports and Literature Requests

Pharmacovigilance

  • Supports Pharmacovigilance (Ovid Alerts, Full Text Articles)

R&D

  • Supports R&D (Document Storage and Retrieval, Literature Searches)

Quality

  • Supports FDA, Health Canada, and DEA audits as needed

Qualifications

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in one of the natural or physical sciences
  • Master’s degree in library and information science preferred
  • Prior work in a library or as a research or editorial assistant or GMP areas
  • Project management experience preferred

Knowledge

  • Possess an understanding of online resource licensing methods and copyright guidelines.
  • Experience updating records in an Integrated Library System (ILS), cataloging, and ILL software such as InMagic/Presto. Experience with the administrative or staff view of an ILS.
  • Familiarity with searching citation databases such as PubMed, OVID, Scifinder, USP, EP, SmartChem, Cortellis, Techstreet.

Skills & Abilities

  • Strong written and verbal communications skills with demonstrated attention to detail, organizational skills, and dedication to quality.
  • Customer focused and self-directed with strong multi-tasking abilities and proven abilities to work well as a part of a team and independently.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel (basic editing / updating / adding and deleting lines). Proficiency with Microsoft SharePoint is a plus.
  • Ability to periodically perform lifting for collection shelving and shifting.
  • Proficiency in current information / library technologies.

Essential Functions

  • Provide access to literature for employees across all platforms and functions, using established workflows.
  • Ensure that metadata records in Presto ILS, and additional internal knowledge management databases are entered correctly and maintained properly.
  • Support the users with literature procurement, access, and organization to meet bibliography and publication requirements.
  • Complete citations for publications as needed, utilizing provided bibliographic tools.
  • Assist with online resource renewals, management, and access.
  • Troubleshoot online journal and resource access as needed.
  • Acquire and process information resources based upon business needs.
  • Maintain and monitor data relating to journal and online resource usage; prepare reports as needed.
  • Facilitate acquisition of lab notebooks / logbooks and their copying / archiving for multiple sites.
  • Edit and distribute electronic Table of Contents and maintain distribution lists.
  • Educate employees on the library’s services and resources.
  • Actively contribute to the maintenance and continuous improvement of our knowledge infrastructure.
  • Manage long-term storage of company files through Iron Mountain
  • Perform other duties as identified and assigned.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift 20-30 pounds and walk across plants and warehouses as needed

description:
Futurex está buscando personas con talento, con pasión por la tecnología e interés por los negocios, para unirse a nuestro equipo de Arquitectos de Soluciones en el puesto de Arquitecto de Soluciones.

El puesto se centra inicialmente en el desarrollo de un profundo conocimiento de la tecnología de Futurex, participando en nuestro proceso de garantía de calidad del software, progresando en la asistencia al cliente y las ventas con organizaciones de nivel 1 en todo el mundo.   • Impartir formación a los clientes sobre nuestros productos y las mejores prácticas de seguridad de datos

Futurex is seeking talented individuals with a passion for technology and an interest in business to join our Solutions Architect team in the position of Solutions Architect. The position is on-site at Futurex’s Mexico City Office.

The Solutions Architect role is a hybrid between business development and IT support. Solutions Architects are as comfortable working with technology as they are with people. The position focuses initially on developing a deep knowledge of Futurex technology by participating in our software quality assurance process, progressing into customer support and sales with Tier-1 organizations worldwide. Responsibilities include:

title: SME Systems Architect
description:
We are seeking a highly accomplished Subject Matter Expert (SME) Systems Engineer to serve as a Senior Digital Transformation Architect & Strategist. In this role, you will define, integrate, and modernize the technical architecture for a centralized enterprise IT systems data ecosystem. You will serve as a strategic technical advisor to executive leadership, bridging the gap between high-level vision and engineering execution.

The ideal candidate will have extensive experience designing secure, scalable architectures that support advanced threat detection, real-time monitoring, automation, predictive analytics, and compliance strategies within complex multi-network Intelligence Community (IC) environments. Specifically, you will lead the architectural evolution and integration of enterprise platform standards including Splunk, ServiceNow, and AppDynamics to drive end-to-end visibility and operational excellence.

  • Future & Integrated Enterprise Architecture: Drive the development, evolution, and alignment of the future-state and integrated technical architecture for critical enterprise platforms, specifically ensuring seamless interoperability between Splunk, ServiceNow, and AppDynamics.
  • Enterprise Technical Architecture: Define and maintain the end-to-end technical architecture for a centralized IT systems data ecosystem, ensuring complete alignment with strategic modernization goals and federal IT mandates.
  • Digital Transformation Leadership: Drive mission enablement for Cyber, IT, and Insight Operations through the deployment of an AI-driven ecosystem that optimizes resources for data-driven success.
  • Strategic Facilitation: Lead and facilitate leadership offsites, multi-agency working groups, and strategic technical discussions to identify and mitigate infrastructure gaps, platform limitations, technical debt, and disconnected workflows.
  • Systems Integration: Lead massive-scale systems integration efforts across disparate technical teams, ensuring seamless integration of Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) and custom-built solutions.
  • Data Governance & Integrity: Build and operationalize robust data governance, data classification, and access control policies across hybrid cloud and on-premise environments in compliance with ICD 503, ICD 504, and upcoming AI mandates (e.g., ICD 505).
  • Security & Compliance Architecture: Architect secure network segmentations, zero-trust frameworks, and cross-domain solutions (CDS) within highly complex security enclaves. Ensure technical systems satisfy strict federal accreditation and assessment (A&A) standards.
  • Technical Mentorship & Governance: Provide technical leadership, conduct comprehensive code/architecture reviews, promote DevSecOps cultures, and establish rigorous performance benchmarks for engineering teams.
  • Program Advisory Support: Assist in managing program scope, schedules, milestones, technical dependencies, and risk mitigation strategies to optimize the return on investment (ROI) for critical technical solutions.

Requirements

  • Required Qualifications
    • Experience:
    • Minimum of 20+ years of technical experience in Systems Engineering, Enterprise Architecture, Systems Integration, and Digital Transformation.
    • Minimum of 15+ years of dedicated experience supporting the Intelligence Community (IC) and/or Department of Defense (DoD).
    • Education: Bachelor’s Degree in Information Technology, Systems Engineering, Business and IT, or a related technical discipline (or equivalent combination of education and experience).
    • Security Clearance: Must possess an active TS/SCI with Polygraph.
  • Required Technical & Core Competencies
    • Enterprise Monitoring & ITSM Integration: Deep architectural understanding and proven ability to support the development of integrated future-state architectures combining Splunk (enterprise logging/SIEM), ServiceNow (ITSM/ITOM), and AppDynamics (application performance monitoring) to deliver holistic operational observability.
    • Architectural Frameworks: Proven expertise using enterprise architecture methodologies (e.g., JARM, Gartner Enterprise Architecture, FEAF) to manage complex system-of-systems configurations.
    • AI/ML Strategy: Broad understanding of the notional AI stack, machine learning lifecycles, full lifecycle model management, and integrating massive enterprise datasets with machine learning tools.
    • Cloud & Infrastructure: Deep familiarity with secure, scalable hybrid cloud engineering solutions (e.g., AWS, cloud-native architectures) and cross-domain communications.
    • Security Standards: Expert-level knowledge of Risk Management Frameworks (RMF), A&A processes, system hardening, and IC directives (including ICD 503, ICD 504, and NIST 800-53 standards).
    • Agile & DevSecOps Mindset: Demonstrated experience championing SecDevOps best practices (automated security testing, IaC, CI/CD pipelines) and working within or across Agile/Scrum delivery teams.
    • Tools: Proficiency utilizing workflow tracking and documentation platforms like JIRA and Confluence to manage system requirements and backlogs.
    • Communication: Exceptional ability to synthesize complex architectural designs and technical issues into high-impact briefings and customer-facing dashboard presentations for senior executive leadership.

title: GCP Data Engineer
description:
• We are looking for an experienced GCP Data Engineer with 5+ years of experience in data engineering and hands‑on expertise in Google Cloud Platform.
  • The candidate will be responsible for implementing, managing, monitoring, and troubleshooting data ingestion pipelines using GCP services.
  • The role requires strong experience with GCS, BigQuery, Dataflow, Cloud Composer, Data Fusion, and Dataproc, along with proficiency in Python, Terraform, and Git.
  • The ideal candidate should be comfortable working independently on data ingestion, ETL/ELT, migration, and production support activities.

Key Responsibilities

  • Configure and execute data ingestion pipelines using reusable GCP‑based frameworks.
  • Develop and manage ETL/ELT workflows using GCS, BigQuery, Dataflow, Composer, Data Fusion, and Dataproc.
  • Manage ingestion parameters, job configurations, metadata, and runtime dependencies.
  • Monitor daily data pipeline executions and ensure agreed SLAs are met.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve data, parameter, configuration, and job execution issues.
  • Analyze runtime failures and independently identify and implement appropriate solutions.
  • Escalate framework‑level defects to the core development team when required.
  • Support data engineering and migration projects on GCP.
  • Develop scripts and automation using Python.
  • Maintain infrastructure configurations and deployment scripts using Terraform.
  • Follow Git‑based version control and deployment best practices.
  • Collaborate with cross‑functional teams to ensure smooth delivery and production operations.
  • Identify opportunities to improve ingestion frameworks, processes, and operational efficiency.
  • Contribute to framework enhancements and automation initiatives where applicable.
  • Work with TWS/TWSd or other enterprise scheduling tools for job scheduling and monitoring, where required.

Mandatory Skills

  • 5+ years of experience as a Data Engineer or in a similar role.
  • Strong hands‑on experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
  • Hands‑on experience with: Google Cloud Storage (GCS) BigQuery Dataflow Cloud Composer Cloud Data Fusion Dataproc Strong Python skills for scripting, debugging, and automation.
  • Experience with Terraform / Infrastructure as Code (IaC).
  • Good understanding of Git and version control.
  • Strong understanding of data ingestion, ETL/ELT workflows, and file formats.
  • Ability to independently troubleshoot and resolve production/runtime data issues.
  • Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills.

Good to Have

  • Experience with TWS/TWSd or other enterprise job scheduling and monitoring tools.
  • Understanding of BigQuery SQL optimization.
  • Experience in GCP data migration projects.
  • Exposure to reusable data ingestion frameworks and production data operations.
  • Preferred Candidate Profile The ideal candidate should be a hands‑on GCP Data Engineer who can independently manage data ingestion pipelines, troubleshoot production issues, work with multiple GCP data services, and support ETL/ELT operations.
  • Strong Python, Terraform, and Git knowledge is expected, along with the ability to work effectively in a production environment.

title: Regional News Director, KMGH, KOAA, KKTV, KKCO & KJCT
description:
Regional News Director, KMGH, KOAA, KKTV, KKCO & KJCT

Are you a transformational news leader ready to shape the future of local journalism across Colorado?

The E.W. Scripps Company is seeking a Regional News Director to lead one of the most important news regions in our company. Based in Denver at KMGH, our ABC affiliate serving Colorado's largest market, this leader will serve as News Director for KMGH while providing strategic leadership and oversight across KOAA (Colorado Springs/Pueblo), KKTV (Colorado Springs), KKCO (Grand Junction), and KJCT (Grand Junction).

This is a unique opportunity for an accomplished newsroom executive to influence journalism, content strategy, audience growth, and newsroom performance across multiple markets while leading a high-performing newsroom in Denver. We are looking for a collaborative, innovative leader who understands how to build strong newsroom cultures, elevate storytelling, develop talent, and leverage the collective strength of multiple stations to better serve audiences across Colorado.

The ideal candidate combines a passion for exceptional local journalism with the strategic vision, leadership skills, and business acumen necessary to guide news operations in a rapidly evolving media landscape.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Create and implement strategic plans for audience growth, journalism excellence, and newsroom operations at KMGH.

  • Communicate a compelling and inspiring vision for the newsroom that aligns with company strategy and content priorities.

  • Develop and execute measurable strategies to grow audiences across broadcast, streaming, digital, and social platforms.

  • Analyze and respond to trends affecting the industry, audience behaviors, competitive landscape, and local news environment.

  • Oversee newsroom staffing and personnel decisions.

  • Develop and manage the annual newsroom budget in accordance with station and company guidelines.

  • Build and maintain key community relationships that strengthen KMGH's reputation and impact.

  • Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, journalistic standards, and company policies.

  • Collaborate with station leadership to achieve overall station and organizational goals.

  • Lead and develop newsroom leaders and staff through coaching, feedback, accountability, and performance management.

  • Partner with station, regional, and corporate leadership to strengthen newsroom performance and align journalistic priorities across KMGH, KOAA, KKTV, KKCO, and KJCT.

  • Identify and lead regional coverage opportunities that leverage the collective strengths, talent, expertise, and resources of Colorado stations.

  • Establish clear performance expectations for market News Directors and provide coaching, mentorship, feedback, and accountability through a dotted-line leadership structure.

  • Evaluate content and journalism across assigned stations to ensure alignment with enterprise content strategy, audience priorities, journalistic standards, and company objectives.

  • Foster collaboration and knowledge sharing across markets to promote best practices and innovation.

  • Partner with station and regional leaders to support workforce planning, resource allocation, and organizational effectiveness across the region.

  • Identify opportunities for shared coverage, breaking news collaboration, investigative initiatives, enterprise reporting, and special projects.

  • Use audience, performance, and operational data to identify opportunities, address challenges, and improve results across markets.

  • Support organizational change and the adoption of emerging technologies, workflows, and content strategies that strengthen local journalism.

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

  • Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Communications, or a related field preferred.

  • 10+ years of progressive news management experience, preferably including leadership of large newsroom operations preferred.

  • Experience leading multiple teams, markets, stations, or geographically dispersed organizations preferred.

  • Demonstrated success driving audience growth and newsroom performance across multiple platforms.

  • Proven experience leading change, developing talent, and building strong newsroom cultures.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

  • A deep commitment to quality local journalism, ethical decision-making, and serving local communities.

  • Demonstrated success developing and executing content strategies that drive audience growth and engagement.

  • Strong strategic thinking and the ability to translate enterprise goals into actionable newsroom plans.

  • Exceptional leadership skills with a track record of empowering teams, establishing accountability, and producing results.

  • Ability to influence and collaborate across organizational boundaries and multiple markets.

  • Strong understanding of audience analytics, content performance metrics, and data-driven decision making.

  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.

  • Proven ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

  • Knowledge of newsroom technology, digital publishing platforms, streaming products, and emerging media trends.

  • Ability to adapt resources, workflows, and talent strategies to meet changing audience expectations and business needs.

  • Strong understanding of journalistic ethics, editorial judgment, and applicable laws affecting news operations.

LOCATION

This position is based in Denver, Colorado, at KMGH-TV. The successful candidate will serve as News Director for KMGH while providing regional leadership for KOAA, KKTV, KKCO, and KJCT. Regular travel throughout Colorado will be expected to support station partnerships, coaching, collaboration, and regional initiatives.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK AND PLAY

Denver offers an unbeatable combination of professional opportunity, cultural vibrancy, and outdoor adventure. With more than 300 days of sunshine each year, residents enjoy easy access to the Rocky Mountains, world-class skiing, hiking, biking, and countless outdoor activities.

As Colorado's largest city, Denver features a thriving downtown, outstanding restaurants, professional sports teams, a vibrant arts and entertainment scene, and a strong economy. From Red Rocks Amphitheatre and the Denver Art Museum to weekend adventures in Vail, Aspen, or Breckenridge, Denver provides an exceptional quality of life and is consistently recognized as one of the nation's best places to live and work.

title: Full-Time Shift Lead – St John, IN
description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly believe in what they are doing. At Dutch Bros Coffee, we are more than just a coffee company. We are a fun-loving, mind-blowing company that makes a difference one cup at a time.

Position Overview

As a Shift Lead, you will ensure that the vision, culture, and core values of Dutch Bros are upheld on every shift. We look to our Shift Leads to be servant leaders within the shop, communicating with leadership on any internal or external feedback. They are the ones who do the hard, and sometimes less desirable, work so that the rest of the crew can focus on core values during shifts.

Job Qualifications

  • 6 months of Broista experience at Dutch Bros preferred

  • No disciplinary action for the past 90 days, required

    • Disciplinary action is defined as a coaching conversation resulting in the completion of formal documentation with signatures

  • Successfully completed the most recent flowcheck (90% score or better) and on time

  • A prerequisite to employment is to obtain and maintain a Food Handler Permit/Certification as required based on state/local regulations

  • Ability to complete, pass and maintain mandatory certificates, training, and knowledge tests under the Dutch Bros required standards for company policies and federal, state, and/or local regulations

Schedule:

  • This role requires that you have availability to work a minimum of 32 hours per week.

  • Available to work a flexible, ever-changing schedule that may include early mornings, evenings, and weekends.

Key Result Area (KRA):

Lead the experience for every Broista on shift that ensures a mind-blowing experience for every customer:

  • Cultivate the Dutch Bros atmosphere and standards on shift ensuring that Broistas are meeting all expectations; help solve problems on shift

  • Manage the shift - responsible for ensuring Broistas are prepared for any specials or promotions and have the right energy and attitude for the customer

Be an expert on drink and operational fundamentals to execute Broista training:

  • Primary responsibility is to model and meet all expectations of the Broista role

  • Train new Broistas operationally and culturally while providing a fun-loving, mind-blowing environment

  • Set Broistas up for success by covering all aspects of the Manifesto during training

Aid your Shop Manager and Shop Lead in shop inventory management, support, and other delegated duties:

  • Set up the next shift for success in all areas: counting tills, bank deposits, restocking products, putting inventory away, meeting cleanliness standards, etc.

  • Communicate with your manager and share wins and opportunities for improvement with your shop leaders

  • Be a good role model. Attend mandatory meetings, know your resources, and adhere to all company policies and procedures as laid out in the Shift Lead Field Guide and Employee Handbook

  • Aid the Shop Manager and Shop Leads in Inventory

  • Aid the Shop Lead and Shop Manager in ensuring shop setup and cleanliness standards are met

  • Work with the Shop Lead and Shop Manager in following up with Quality Assurance inspections and accountability process

Levels of Leadership Expectations

Anchor Points

  • Excellent Communicator: Communicate appropriate information up to your leaders, and communicate expectations to the crew while on shift.

  • Available: You must be able to work shift lead shifts and be present at shop meetings and culture building events.

Level-Up Arrow:

Effort + Skill x Attitude = Performance

  • Effort: Giving it your all! Wanting more for yourself and for others. Going above and beyond your own perceived capabilities.

  • Skill: Being a master at the craft. Having high emotional intelligence and a great understanding of people. Keeping a mindset and heart to be a student of the game.

  • Attitude: Have an attitude that is unshakeable. Be resilient and optimistic. “To be so strong that nothing can disturb your peace of mind.

* You must also demonstrate all Broista Levels of Leadership expectations (anchors and level-up arrows).

Employee Benefits & Perks

  • Free Dutch Bros swag

  • Free coffee per Employee Drink Policy

  • Paid volunteer hours

  • Employee Assistance Program

  • Access to our Financial Wellness Platform

  • 401(k) eligibility after 1 year of employment

  • Education Benefit Program after 1 year of employment

Full-time shift lead also receives:

  • Employer-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Sick time, as applicable by state law

  • Paid time off

  • Paid holidays (6 per year)

*More details on all benefits provided after onboarding

Physical Requirements

  • Constant standing/walking, up to 10 hours at a time

  • Occasional stooping, kneeling, or crawling

  • Occasional pushing, pulling, lifting, or carrying up to 65 lbs

  • Possible exposure to extreme heat and/or cold temperatures

  • Occasional ascending or descending on ladders and ramps

  • Frequent, continual, intermittent flexing, or rotation of the wrist(s) and spine

  • Constantly receiving detailed information through oral communication

  • Constant clarity of vision at near and/or far distances

  • Constant cash handling requiring mental math

  • Constant talking, expressing, or exchanging ideas by means of verbal communication

*Qualifying candidates may be eligible to receive relocation compensation upon acceptance of a job offer that requires them to move. The amount of relocation compensation varies and is based on the total distance of the relocation (among other variables).

Compensation:

Up to $17.25 per hour

description:
Now that you’ve found the job description, what’s next?

At icebreaker and Smartwool, we are two unique brands that embody the same spirit of belonging, adventure, sustainability, and getting out there. We create products made for people who enjoy nature and want to go far and feel good. We do this all while keeping our planet and the impact of our products in mind.

So, before we get to the job details, take a minute to learn a little more about us – our values and our culture. If you can see yourself working side-by-side with a team of fun, adventure-loving people, icebreaker and Smartwool may be just the place for you.

To learn more about our values and our culture, visit or .

Senior Supply Planner (Smartwool & icebreaker)

What will you do?

A day in the life of a Sr Supply Planner at icebreaker and Smartwool looks a little like this.

You will play a critical role in achieving financial targets by procuring supply to meet service and inventory objectives. You will ensure on-time delivery from vendors through close partnership with Global Supply Planning, Sourcing, Logistics, Demand Planning, Distribution, and Customer Service, while proactively managing capacity constraints and supply risks.

Let’s break down that day-in-the-life a bit more.

  • Own category-level supply planning and buy recommendations using demand inputs, current inventory, lead times, vendor capacity, MOQs/pack sizes, and buy readiness; create and route purchase requisitions in SAP to the Global Supply Planning team for execution.

  • Provide monthly supply outlook and Open-to-Buy inputs to Inventory Planning for assigned categories, including expected receipts, inventory position, and risks/opportunities.

  • Monitor demand and supply timing on an ongoing basis using SAP and Excel-based trackers; identify exceptions (potential stockouts, excess, past-due supply) and re-phase supply to improve customer service and meet inventory objectives.

  • Partner with Demand Planning during capacity or material constraints to align forecasts to feasible supply, recommend prioritization, and communicate impacts to availability.

  • Manage seasonal system set-up and line plan validation in partnership with Demand Planning, ensuring item readiness, assumptions alignment, and correct timing for seasonal flows.

  • Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders (Demand Planning, Inventory Planning, Finance, Commercial/Merchandising, Operations, Global Supply Planning) to support delivery of current-month financial objectives while balancing service, inventory, and cost.

  • Support service and inventory performance reporting with the Inventory Analyst; analyze trends and exceptions and drive follow-up actions to improve operational performance and business outcomes.

  • Provide department leadership and planning expertise to other planners and adjacent teams; recommend and implement process improvements, standard work, and planning best practices (SAP execution and Excel analysis).

  • Maintain a longer-term view of supply availability across assigned categories by product type; assess capacity, vendor constraints, and material risks, and recommend mitigation actions (timing shifts, pre-buys, prioritization, alternatives).

  • Participate in and/or lead key projects to evolve supply chain capabilities, including improvements to planning processes, SAP utilization, and Excel-based reporting/analytics.

  • Perform ad hoc analysis and reporting as required to support leadership decisions, issue resolution, and continuous improvement initiatives.

What do you need to succeed?

We all have unique skills that we bring to work and celebrate every day. For this role, there are foundation skills you’ll need to succeed and excel. Additionally, while formal education in a related field is great to have (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent from four-year college or university with a concentration in Supply Chain or Business Management)), we are most interested in your 3+ years of experience in a corporate supply chain environment, ideally in demand & supply planning.

The foundation skills you will need in this position are:

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

  • Ability to understand, assess, & problem solve by leveraging technical and analytical skills

  • Ability to work effectively within a cross-functional team environment

  • Proven ability to multi-task effectively

  • Advanced Excel Skills (pivot tables, macro’s)

  • Understanding of reporting tools (Brio/SAP Business Objects/PowerBI)

  • Experience in project planning and implementation

  • Self-starter with excellent follow through

  • Excellent attention to detail

  • SAP System experience, a plus

  • Travel estimated at 5% or less of the time
