title: Associate Director/Director Public Health & Community Partnerships
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
JOB TITLE: Associate Director/Director Public Health & Community Partnerships

REPORTS TO: VP of Public Health & Government Affairs

DEPARTMENT: Corporate Strategy

HOURS: Monday – Friday 9-5

FLSA STATUS: Exempt

JOB TYPE: Full-Time

Location: New York – Hybrid
Travel: Approximately 30–50%

RATE: 100k -135k (Dependent on Experience)

About Healthix
Healthix is the largest public health information exchange (HIE) in New York State, securely connecting thousands of healthcare providers, hospitals, health plans, and community organizations to improve the quality, safety, and efficiency of care. Through the secure exchange of health information, Healthix helps ensure that clinicians, care teams, and public health partners have access to the data they need to make informed decisions and deliver better outcomes for the communities they serve.

As part of our ongoing organizational transformation, Healthix is expanding its focus beyond data exchange to making health information more actionable and impactful for healthcare providers, community partners, and public health initiatives. This transformation reflects our commitment to strengthening community partnerships, improving health equity, and supporting innovative approaches that connect healthcare with community-based services.

Through initiatives such as Healthix Connects, our internal volunteer and community engagement program, we are deepening our relationships with local organizations and creating opportunities for our team to actively support healthier, safer communities.

Joining Healthix means becoming part of a mission-driven organization that is shaping the future of health information sharing while building stronger connections between healthcare systems and the communities they serve.

The Role

The Director, Public Health & Community Partnerships will support the development and execution of Healthix's public health strategy, using data, research, and strategic partnerships to advance initiatives that improve population health and healthcare outcomes across New York communities.

Reporting to the Vice President of Public Health & Government Affairs, the Director will build relationships with public health agencies, healthcare organizations, community-based organizations, academic and research institutions, health plans, payers, and other stakeholders to identify emerging health needs and opportunities for collaboration.

The Director will combine Healthix's longitudinal healthcare data with public health, population, demographic, environmental, and other relevant data and research to support studies, programs, and initiatives that provide meaningful insight into health outcomes, disparities, healthcare utilization, resource availability, and healthcare costs.

A critical responsibility of the role will be translating these insights into compelling, actionable information that can educate and influence policymakers, healthcare leaders, providers, insurers, health plans, payers, community leaders, and other decision-makers and contribute to strategies that improve health outcomes and the allocation of healthcare resources.

Key Responsibilities

Public Health Strategy & Programs

  • Partner with the Vice President of Public Health & Government Affairs to develop and execute Healthix's public health, population health, health equity, and community engagement strategy.
  • Monitor public health priorities and emerging health trends across New York City, Long Island, and New York State and identify opportunities where Healthix's data and partnerships can contribute to solutions.
  • Develop and support studies, programs, and collaborative initiatives addressing areas such as population health, health equity, chronic disease, maternal health, behavioral and mental health, environmental health, healthcare access, and social drivers of health.
  • Apply knowledge of public health data, epidemiology, biostatistics, and health economics to evaluate population trends, health outcomes, disease burden, healthcare utilization, resource availability, and healthcare costs.
  • Examine the relationship between health outcomes and environmental, social, behavioral, and economic factors affecting the populations Healthix serves.

Data, Research & Impact

  • Collaborate with Healthix's data and technical teams and external partners to use Healthix's longitudinal data and other relevant data sources to support public health studies and initiatives.
  • Gather, evaluate, and synthesize public health, population, demographic, healthcare utilization, cost, and community-level data to identify trends, disparities, risks, and opportunities.
  • Translate complex data and research findings into clear insights, presentations, reports, recommendations, and compelling narratives for technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Develop meaningful measures and outcomes to demonstrate the impact of public health initiatives and partnerships.
  • Identify opportunities where Healthix's data can provide new insight into population health challenges and support evidence-based decision-making.

Partnerships & Influence

  • Develop meaningful relationships with public health agencies, healthcare providers, health systems, health plans, payers, insurers, academic and research institutions, community-based organizations, advocacy organizations, and other stakeholders throughout New York.
  • Use these relationships to identify opportunities for collaborative research, public health programs, funding, and community initiatives.
  • Bring together Healthix data, external expertise, and strategic partners to develop initiatives capable of driving measurable public health impact.
  • Present findings and recommendations to government, healthcare, and community stakeholders to educate, inform, and influence decisions related to healthcare policy, programs, resource allocation, access, and investment.
  • Represent Healthix at public health forums, community meetings, conferences, coalitions, and stakeholder discussions.

Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Public Health, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Health Economics, Population Health, Health Policy, or related field strongly preferred.
  • 5+ years of experience in public health, population health, healthcare, research, government, academic, nonprofit, or related environments.
  • Demonstrated experience working with public health and population-level data, including the ability to interpret statistical and epidemiological findings.
  • Working knowledge of biostatistics, epidemiology, health economics, healthcare utilization, and healthcare cost concepts.
  • Knowledge of health equity, environmental and social drivers of health, and behavioral and mental health.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate data and research into actionable insights and communicate findings effectively to diverse stakeholders and decision-makers.
  • Proven ability to develop partnerships across healthcare, government, public health, academic, and community organizations.
  • Strong presentation, writing, analytical, relationship-building, and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Experience with healthcare data, health information exchange, clinical data, claims, Medicaid populations, or real-world healthcare data is highly desirable.
  • Must reside in New York State and demonstrate meaningful knowledge of and professional or community connections within New York City, Long Island, or surrounding New York communities.

title: Director Practice Operations (LCMC Ruidoso)
location: Lincoln County Medical Center - White Mountain Clinic
description:
Location Address:

129 El Paso Rd
Ruidoso, NM 88345-6033


Summary:

Presbyterian Medical Group (PMG) seeks a transformational ambulatory healthcare leader to serve as its next Director of Practice Operations. This highly visible leadership role is responsible for operational, financial, service, and people performance across a portfolio of physician and advanced practice provider clinics.

As healthcare continues to evolve toward value-based care, consumerism, digital engagement, and integrated care delivery models, PMG is investing in operational leaders who can move beyond traditional practice management and serve as strategic business partners to physicians, advanced practice providers, and clinical leaders.

The Director will lead the execution of ambulatory strategies designed to improve access, provider productivity, patient experience, workforce engagement, quality outcomes, and financial performance. This leader will work closely with physician leaders, practice managers, operational executives, and support service departments to create high-performing outpatient operations that deliver exceptional care and sustainable growth.

The ideal candidate is a collaborative healthcare operator who combines strong business acumen, physician partnership skills, operational discipline, and a passion for improving both patient and provider experiences.

Job Description:

Operational Leadership & Performance Management

  • Provide leadership and oversight for assigned ambulatory practices and service lines.

  • Establish operational strategies that align with organizational priorities and growth objectives.

  • Drive performance across key operational metrics including access, provider utilization, productivity, patient throughput, and service levels.

  • Develop operational action plans that improve efficiency, capacity, and patient outcomes.

  • Create accountability structures that support performance excellence across all sites.

Physician & Provider Partnership

  • Serve as a strategic business partner to physicians, advanced practice providers, and medical leadership.

  • Collaborate with clinical leaders to optimize provider productivity, panel management, scheduling templates, and access strategies.

  • Support physician engagement, provider satisfaction, and workforce retention efforts.

  • Facilitate alignment between operational priorities and clinical goals.

  • Foster a collaborative, physician-friendly culture focused on delivering exceptional care.

Financial Stewardship

  • Lead development and execution of annual operating plans and budgets.

  • Manage financial performance across assigned practices, including revenue, expenses, productivity, and operating margin.

  • Monitor key financial indicators and implement strategies that improve fiscal performance.

  • Identify opportunities for growth, operational efficiency, and resource optimization.

  • Support business planning and evaluation of new services, programs, and growth opportunities.

Access, Growth & Consumer Experience

  • Lead initiatives that improve patient access, scheduling efficiency, and capacity management.

  • Develop strategies that enhance patient acquisition, retention, and loyalty.

  • Improve consumer experience through service excellence and operational innovation.

  • Monitor patient satisfaction metrics and implement improvements that enhance care delivery.

  • Partner with marketing and business development teams to support growth initiatives.

Quality, Safety & Regulatory Excellence

  • Ensure compliance with organizational policies, accreditation standards, and regulatory requirements.

  • Support quality improvement and patient safety initiatives across ambulatory operations.

  • Utilize data and performance metrics to improve quality outcomes and operational effectiveness.

  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement and accountability.

  • Partner with quality and clinical teams to monitor performance against organizational goals.

Workforce Leadership & Culture

  • Lead, coach, and develop practice managers and operational leaders.

  • Build high-performing teams focused on accountability, engagement, and service excellence.

  • Support workforce planning, succession planning, and talent development initiatives.

  • Promote a culture aligned with Presbyterian values and leadership expectations.

  • Implement strategies that improve employee engagement, retention, and professional growth.

Strategic Planning & Transformation

  • Lead strategic and tactical planning initiatives for assigned practices.

  • Identify opportunities to improve workflows, leverage technology, and enhance operational performance.

  • Drive change management efforts related to new programs, services, and organizational initiatives.

  • Partner with enterprise leaders to implement ambulatory transformation strategies.

  • Evaluate emerging healthcare trends and recommend innovative approaches to care delivery.

Data Analytics & Performance Improvement

  • Utilize operational, clinical, financial, and patient experience data to drive decision-making.

  • Develop performance dashboards and reporting mechanisms for leaders and providers.

  • Monitor KPIs and establish action plans to address performance gaps.

  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives using data-driven methodologies.

  • Benchmark performance against industry standards and best practices.

Success Measures

Within the first 12–24 months, the Director will be expected to:

  • Improve patient access and reduce appointment wait times across assigned practices.

  • Achieve targeted provider productivity and panel management goals.

  • Improve patient satisfaction and consumer experience metrics.

  • Enhance financial performance through operational efficiency, growth, and expense management.

  • Strengthen physician, APP, and employee engagement scores.

  • Reduce operational variation and standardize best practices across practices.

  • Successfully implement strategic growth and operational transformation initiatives.

  • Improve quality, safety, and regulatory performance metrics.

  • Establish a data-driven culture that supports accountability and continuous improvement.

  • Build high-performing operational teams capable of sustaining long-term success.

Additional Job Description:

Education

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, Public Health, Nursing, or a related field.

Preferred

  • Master's degree in Healthcare Administration (MHA), Business Administration (MBA), Public Health, or related discipline.

Experience

Required

  • 7–10 years of progressive healthcare leadership experience.

  • Minimum of 5 years leading ambulatory, physician practice, medical group, or outpatient operations.

  • Demonstrated experience managing multiple practices, service lines, or operational departments.

  • Experience leading operational, financial, workforce, and patient experience improvement initiatives.

  • Strong understanding of ambulatory operations, practice management, access management, and provider productivity.

Benefits
Benefits are effective day-one (for .45 FTE and above) and include:

  • Competitive salaries
  • Full medical, dental and vision insurance
  • Flexible spending accounts (FSAs)
  • Free wellness programs
  • Paid time off (PTO)
  • Retirement plans, including matching employer contributions
  • Continuing education and career development opportunities
  • Life insurance and short/long term disability programs

About Us
Presbyterian Healthcare Services is a locally owned, not-for-profit healthcare system of nine hospitals, a statewide health plan and a growing multi-specialty medical group. Founded in New Mexico in 1908, it is the state's largest private employer with approximately 11,000 employees.

Presbyterian's story is really the story of the remarkable people who have chosen to work here. Starting with Reverend Cooper who began our journey in 1908, the hard work of thousands of physicians, employees, board members, and other volunteers brought Presbyterian from a tiny tuberculosis sanatorium to a statewide healthcare system, serving more than 700,000 New Mexicans.

We are part of New Mexico's history - and committed to its future. That is why we will continue to work just as hard and care just as deeply to serve New Mexico for years to come.

About New Mexico
New Mexico's unique blend of Spanish, Mexican and Native American influences contribute to a culturally rich lifestyle. Add in Albuquerque's International Balloon Fiesta, Los Alamos' nuclear scientists, Roswell's visitors from outer space, and Santa Fe's artists, and you get an eclectic mix of people, places and experiences that make this state great.

Cities in New Mexico are continually ranked among the nation's best places to work and live by Forbes magazine, Kiplinger's Personal Finance, and other corporate and government relocation managers like Worldwide ERC.

New Mexico offers endless recreational opportunities to explore, and enjoy an active lifestyle. Venture off the beaten path, challenge your body in the elements, or open yourself up to the expansive sky. From hiking, golfing and biking to skiing, snowboarding and boating, it's all available among our beautiful wonders of the west.

AA/EOE/VET/DISABLED. PHS is a drug-free and tobacco-free employer with smoke free campuses.

title: Director, Brand Management
description:
Grow with us...

Life at Starwood Hotels is based on a simple idea: the world is beautiful and we want to keep it that way. But we can’t do it alone. That’s why hiring thoughtful and inspiring Team Members and Leaders who understand that our people, collaboration, stellar service, and respect for nature are so important to us.

It’s an exciting time at Starwood Hotels as we have significant global expansion underway with locations such as Cabo, Dubai, Maldives, and beyond, in our future! With our growth comes new opportunities to hire even more extraordinary people as we branch out into new territories.

Here’s what we’re currently looking for: Director, Brand Management.

What is this role all about?

The Director of Brand Management is a key member of the Home Office Brand Marketing team for Starwood Hotels and its brands around the world. This role is responsible for evolving and activating brand positioning across all aspects of the guest journey, ensuring the brand is expressed consistently and meaningfully across experiences, communications, and marketing channels.

This individual leads brand pull-through across key touchpoints of the customer experience and helps define the strategic proof points, concepts, and initiatives that bring each brand to life as the portfolio grows globally. The role also identifies opportunities to infuse the brand experience with new and innovative thinking, including emerging technologies, shifting consumer expectations, and cultural trends.

Serving as a key liaison between Brand Marketing, Operations, and other critical Home Office corporate teams, this role helps ensure brand strategy is translated into clear, actionable standards and experiences across the organization. Working closely with cross-functional partners, including the Creative team, this individual ensures execution remains on strategy and aligned with the brand vision across the full customer journey.

The individual in this role serves as the voice of the target consumer, representing the brand vision in all aspects of the experiences we create and deliver.

BRAND STRATEGY & POSITIONING

  • Define, evolve, and articulate the brand positioning for each brand, ensuring clear strategic direction across guest-facing and internal touchpoints.
  • Serve as a steward of the brand vision, ensuring it is expressed consistently across the customer journey, team member experience, and brand communications.
  • Identify opportunities to strengthen and modernize the brand through innovation, emerging technologies, consumer insights, and cultural trends.
  • Develop and refine brand proof points, experience concepts, and strategic initiatives that support portfolio growth and differentiation.

BRAND OPERATIONS & CROSS-FUNCTIONAL LEADERSHIP

  • Act as a key liaison between Brand Marketing, Operations, and other critical Home Office teams to ensure brand strategy is effectively translated into operational standards and execution.
  • Partner with Operations, Procurement, and Design on OS&E development and standardization, uniform design and development, and other physical brand touchpoints.
  • Lead the development and ongoing evolution of brand standards in collaboration with Operations and People Operations.
  • Support key cross-functional initiatives such as brand immersions, training content, employer branding, mentorship, DEI-related programming, and other team member experience efforts.
  • Build strong relationships across the organization to align stakeholders, drive progress, and embed brand thinking into decision-making.

GUEST EXPERIENCE & PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT

  • Shape the end-to-end customer journey by identifying and developing branded experience touchpoints and proof points.
  • Lead the development of signature guest experience programs, such as sustainability pull-through, family programming, pet programming, and other brand-defining initiatives.
  • Ensure that all aspects of the experience reflect the brand in thoughtful, differentiated, and operationally viable ways.
  • Champion the philosophy that everything communicates, guiding how the brand is expressed across physical, digital, service, and experiential touchpoints.

CREATIVE STEWARDSHIP

  • Partner closely with the Creative team to ensure all creative output reflects the brand strategy, positioning, and guest experience vision.
  • Provide strategic brand direction and feedback on creative materials, campaigns, presentations, and brand expressions across channels and touchpoints.
  • Ensure creative execution remains aligned with established brand standards, voice, and positioning.
  • Collaborate with the Assistant Director and Creative partners on brand tools and assets that support property needs, openings, new initiatives, and cross-functional business priorities.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS

  • 10+ years of relevant experience in brand management, brand marketing, or experience strategy, ideally within luxury, lifestyle, hospitality, or consumer brands.
  • Proven experience developing and evolving brand positioning and translating it into meaningful consumer and team member experiences.
  • Strong understanding of brand strategy, marketing, guest experience, and the role of operational touchpoints in bringing a brand to life.
  • Experience partnering cross-functionally with Operations, Design, Procurement, People Operations, Digital, and Marketing teams.
  • Ability to influence and drive alignment across a matrixed organization through strong relationships, sound judgment, and clear communication.
  • Experience guiding creative development from a brand strategy perspective, ensuring work is on-brand and aligned to positioning.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present ideas clearly and professionally to a range of stakeholders.
  • Strong attention to detail and a high bar for quality and consistency across all brand expressions.

Experience in the luxury and/or lifestyle space is required.

  • Collaborative, thoughtful, and team-oriented approach.
  • Must possess legal authorization to work in the United States.

Salary: $160,000

About us...

As a mission-driven company, our purpose is our true north, and our compass guides the way. The purpose we live by impacts the lives of our team members, drives the experiences for our guests, builds community with like-minded travelers and takes care of the planet we live in. Founded in 2006 by Barry Sternlicht, Starwood Hotels is a luxury hotel brand management company and affiliate of global private investment firm Starwood Capital Group.

Starwood Hotels is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We believe in a diverse, sustainable workforce with an empowered, inclusive culture. We are committed to non-discrimination on any protected basis covered under applicable law. If you require any special accommodations, please visit People Operations.

title: Archaeologist/Archaeological Monitor (Puerto Rico)
description:
Title: Archaeologist (Monitor)
Location: Puerto Rico
Job Code: SOI-PR-26
Job Link: SEARCH Job Postings - Direct Applications

Position Information

SEARCH has an immediate opening for on-call Archaeologists to join our Terrestrial Archaeology division for monitoring projects in Puerto Rico. Selected candidates must be Secretary of the Interior Qualified in Archaeology and based in Puerto Rico, with knowledge on island cultural resources. In addition to monitoring projects, archaeologists may be called to participate in SEARCH survey projects around the island.

The formal title of this role is that of an Archaeological Technician, though the advertised title reflects the job function for consideration. Rotation schedules depend on project needs but are typically 10/4s, 6/1s or 5/2s. Starting hourly wage ranges from $20-$22 per hour, commensurate with education and experience. Travel time is paid, including mid-project travel for breaks. Travel days are considered part of the rotation. Lodging is single room accommodations and SEARCH pays per diem (no receipts needed) at a usual rate of $50/night and $25 on demobilization days when staying away from home.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Adhere to project health and safety plans and participate in office and field trainings and meetings.
  • Conduct archaeological monitoring, survey, testing, and excavation in support of Phase I, II, and III studies in accordance with the research design to identify, record, and evaluate historic and prehistoric cultural resources.
  • Recognize archaeological signatures and apply reasoning to evaluate resources.
  • Evaluate and record accurate, organized, and clear field notes, maps, drawings, logs, forms, tables, databases, artifact bags, box labels, and other project documentation.
  • Collect and inventory artifacts, ecofacts, and samples in accordance with the research design, and keep an accurate field specimen log.
  • Identify potential human and faunal remains, and treat any suspected human burial remains respectfully and in a manner consistent with the research design and applicable State and Federal guidelines and laws.
  • Perform quality control of field data (hand-written and electronic) on a daily basis to ensure information is accurate and complete.
  • Use electronic and traditional navigational equipment (GPS, iPad/ArcCollector/Survey 123, compass, transit, etc.) to determine project limits, record fieldwork, document findings, and communicate progress.
  • Photo-document artifacts, features, excavation units, land use, landscapes, unique environmental features, historic structures, archaeology sites, unique environmental features, specialized equipment or technique usage, and work-in-progress.
  • Procure and maintain field equipment, technology, field laboratory supplies, vehicles, and supplies in a clean, working, and safe manner.
  • Occasionally meet with, coordinate, and collaborate with landowners, land agents, clients, other field research teams, and visiting regulatory agency staff.
  • Travel for extended periods of time.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Requirements

Qualifications Required:

  • Graduate degree in Anthropology, Archaeology, or a related field.
  • Meet the Secretary of the Interior (SOI) qualifications for archaeology.
  • Live in Puerto Rico at time of hire.
  • Experience with Caribbean archaeology.
  • Ability to perform physically demanding tasks in variable terrain and environments.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • A valid driver’s license and access to reliable transportation.
  • Demonstrative knowledge of and familiarity with performing archaeological monitoring, survey and excavation.


Application Requirements

  • Cover letter
  • Resume
  • Cover Letter
  • References


Other Important Need-to-Know Information

  • This position will require flexible availability outside of standard working hours.
  • Applicants must be eligible to be employed in the United States on federally contracted projects.
  • SEARCH is strongly committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment where a variety of backgrounds, cultures, orientations, ideas, and talents can flourish.
  • SEARCH is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.
  • SEARCH is an Affirmative Action Employer and a Drug-Free Workplace.
  • Employment offers are contingent upon satisfactory verification of criminal, education, driving, and/or employment background checks as well as passing results from a pre-employment drug screen.
  • We will endeavor to make a reasonable accommodation to the known limitations of a qualified applicant with a disability unless the accommodation would impose an undue hardship on the operation of our business. If you believe you require such assistance to complete this form or, if requested, to participate in an interview, please let us know.

Benefits

About SEARCH:

SEARCH is a global leader in archaeology, maritime archaeology, and the full spectrum of cultural heritage services. SEARCH’s staff are industry leaders and subject matter experts who support commercial and government clients worldwide. Since 1993, SEARCH has completed over 5,000 projects nationwide and across 44 countries, spanning seven continents and four oceans. By integrating science, technology, and creativity, SEARCH harnesses the power of the past to advance the projects, places, and people it serves.

For more information about SEARCH, please visit and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and Twitter.

Please send inquiries about the position to jorge.quintana@searchinc.com. Include the Job Posting code (SOI-PR-26) in the subject line of your email.

title: Incident Response Analyst - Americas
description:
Company Profile

The Carlyle Group (NASDAQ: CG) is a global investment firm with $485 billion of assets under management, across 678 investment vehicles as of June 30, 2026. Founded in 1987 in Washington, DC, Carlyle has grown into one of the world's largest and most successful investment firms, with more than 2,500 professionals operating in 28 offices in North America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Australia.

Carlyle’s purpose is to connect people, ideas, and capital to fuel growth for companies and performance for investors, which range from public and private pension funds to wealthy individuals and families to sovereign wealth funds, unions and corporations. Carlyle invests across three segments – Global Private Equity, Global Credit and Carlyle AlpInvest – and has deep expertise across industries, markets, and geographies.

At Carlyle, we believe that a wide spectrum of experiences and viewpoints drives performance and success. Our CEO, Harvey Schwartz, has stated that, "To build better businesses and create value for all of our stakeholders, we are focused on assembling leadership teams with the strongest insights from a range of perspectives." Reflecting this view, emphasis is placed on development, retention and inclusion through our internal processes and seven Employee Resource Groups (ERGs). We cultivate a culture where ideas are openly shared and challenged, connecting diverse expertise and perspectives to drive enduring value.

Position Summary

The Incident Response Analyst plays a critical role in protecting the organization’s information, technology platforms, and sensitive financial data from increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. This is a hands-on technical position within the Security Operations Center (SOC), responsible for investigating, containing, and resolving security incidents across endpoint, identity, network, cloud, SaaS, and enterprise environments. The successful candidate will combine strong cybersecurity fundamentals with modern detection, investigation, automation, and threat analysis capabilities to rapidly identify malicious activity and reduce organizational risk.

The ideal candidate will possess a strong understanding of incident response, security operations, threat detection, threat hunting, and digital investigation methodologies. They will take ownership of security incidents throughout the response lifecycle, including triage, investigation, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident analysis. The analyst will correlate and analyze telemetry from multiple security technologies—including SIEM, XDR, EDR, identity, network, cloud, email, and data protection platforms—to reconstruct attack activity, determine scope and impact, identify root cause, and recommend appropriate remediation actions. Familiarity with contemporary attack techniques and frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK is essential for understanding adversary behavior and improving detection and response capabilities.

This role will be an advocate for an automation-first SOC. The Incident Response Analyst will leverage security orchestration, scripting, APIs, automation platforms, and increasingly AI-assisted security capabilities to accelerate investigations and reduce repetitive manual activities. The analyst should be comfortable identifying opportunities to automate enrichment, evidence collection, alert triage, containment actions, case management, and other repeatable incident response processes while maintaining appropriate human oversight for high-impact decisions.

As enterprise environments increasingly span traditional infrastructure and cloud services, the analyst must understand modern attack surfaces across endpoints, identities, networks, cloud infrastructure, SaaS platforms, applications, and data environments. Knowledge of cloud security concepts, identity-based attacks, credential compromise, privilege escalation, lateral movement, data exfiltration, ransomware, phishing, malware, and emerging AI-enabled threats will be important to effectively investigate and respond to modern cyberattacks.

The Incident Response Analyst will also contribute to the continuous improvement of the SOC by performing threat hunting, detection engineering, incident retrospectives, playbook development, and security control optimization. Lessons learned from investigations should be translated into improved detections, automated workflows, response procedures, and preventative controls. The analyst will work closely with security engineering, threat intelligence, vulnerability management, identity, cloud, infrastructure, application security, and other technology teams to strengthen the organization's overall detection and response capabilities.

Strong communication and sound judgment are equally important. During significant security incidents, the analyst must clearly communicate technical findings, business impact, response actions, and recommendations to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. They must be capable of managing multiple investigations, making risk-based decisions with incomplete information, maintaining accurate incident documentation and evidence, and remaining effective during high-pressure situations.

This position provides an opportunity to work with modern security technologies and help shape the evolution of a data-driven, intelligence-led, and highly automated Security Operations Center. The successful candidate will demonstrate technical curiosity, analytical thinking, ownership, collaboration, and a continuous-improvement mindset while helping the organization detect threats earlier, investigate incidents faster, and respond to cyber threats more effectively.

In-Office Requirement: 4 days per week

Primary Responsibilities

Security Incident Response

  • Analyze, investigate, document, contain, remediate, and coordinate response to cybersecurity incidents across endpoint, identity, network, cloud, SaaS, email, application, and data environments. Maintain ownership of incidents through resolution and ensure appropriate escalation, communication, evidence preservation, and documentation throughout the incident lifecycle.

SOC Escalation and Advanced Investigation

  • Serve as an escalation point for security events referred by the Tier 1 Managed Security Service Provider (MSSP) that require deeper technical analysis, validation, or response. Correlate telemetry across multiple security platforms to determine attack scope, root cause, affected identities and assets, potential business impact, and required containment or remediation actions.

Detection Engineering

  • Develop, test, tune, and continuously improve detection logic, correlation rules, analytics, queries, and behavioral detections designed to identify advanced and emerging threats. Translate lessons learned from incidents and threat hunting activities into improved detection and prevention capabilities.

Security Automation and AI-Assisted Operations

  • Identify opportunities to automate repetitive investigation and response activities using scripting, APIs, security orchestration, workflow automation, and AI-assisted security technologies. Develop and improve automated workflows for alert enrichment, evidence collection, investigation, case management, containment, and remediation while maintaining appropriate human oversight.

Incident Response Playbooks

  • Develop, maintain, test, and continuously improve incident response playbooks and operational procedures for common and high-impact security scenarios, including compromised accounts, phishing, malware, ransomware, data exfiltration, insider threats, cloud compromise, and other emerging attack techniques.

Metrics and Reporting

  • Develop and maintain meaningful operational metrics and reporting related to incident response, detection effectiveness, threat hunting, automation, project deliverables, and SOC performance. Use operational data to identify trends and opportunities to improve detection coverage, response time, and overall security effectiveness.

Continuous Learning and Technical Leadership

  • Maintain and expand technical expertise through research, hands-on lab work, threat research, training, industry engagement, and professional development. Share knowledge with other analysts, mentor team members, document technical findings, and contribute to improving the overall capabilities and maturity of the Security Operations Center.

Requirements

Education & Certificates

  • Four-year college degree, or equivalent years’ of relevant experience, required.
  • Certifications in incident response (GCIH, SANS) or security (CISSP, CCSP) preferred.

Professional Experience

  • 5+ years of overall IT-related experience, required.
  • 3+ years of IT security operations and incident response experience, required.
  • Knowledge of financial services industry and alternative asset management, strongly preferred.
  • In-depth knowledge of incident response methodologies (identify, contain, eradicate, recover, learn).
  • Proven ability to conduct investigations, analyze evidence, and identify root causes of security incidents.
  • Experience with digital forensics and evidence collection techniques in various environments (cloud, network, endpoint).
  • Experience with leveraging APIs to automate integrations between security tools.
  • Knowledge of cloud security best practices (IAM, encryption, logging).
  • Ability to prioritize tasks, manage multiple incidents concurrently, and work effectively under pressure.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills to diagnose complex security incidents.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills to work effectively with security teams, IT teams, and business stakeholders.

Position-specific Technical Requirements

  • Proficiency with security orchestration, automation and response (SOAR) platforms (Palo Alto XSIAM).
  • Proficiency with security information and event management (SIEM) tools
  • Proficiency with at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure)
  • Familiarity with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools (Terraform, CloudFormation).
  • Experience with scripting languages (Python, Bash, PowerShell) for automating incident response tasks.
  • Strong understanding of network security concepts (firewalls, intrusion detection/prevention systems).
  • Proficiency with endpoint security tools (antivirus, endpoint detection and response (EDR), Application Control.
  • Working knowledge of various operating systems (Windows, Linux, macOS).

Benefits/Compensation

The compensation range for this role is specific to Washington, DC and takes into account a wide range of factors including but not limited to the skill sets required/preferred; prior experience and training; licenses and/or certifications.

The anticipated base salary range for this role is $140,000-$160,000.

In addition to the base salary, the hired professional will enjoy a comprehensive benefits package spanning retirement benefits, health insurance, life insurance and disability, paid time off, paid holidays, family planning benefits and various wellness programs. Additionally, the hired professional may also be eligible to participate in an annual discretionary incentive program, the award of which will be dependent on various factors, including, without limitation, individual and organizational performance.

Due to the high volume of candidates, please be advised that only candidates selected to interview will be contacted by Carlyle.

title: Broista – Amelia, OH
description:

At Dutch Bros Coffee, we are a fun-loving, mind-blowing company, making a massive difference one cup at a time.

  • Embody. Live out the Dutch Bros values: radiate kindness, get up early, stay up late, and change the world.
  • Stay Fast & Focused. Work efficiently to craft high-quality drinks while keeping up with the hustle of a busy shop.
  • Be Reliable. Show up on time, communicate your availability, and be ready to roll when your shift starts.
  • Keep it Clean. Maintain a tidy workspace and follow food safety standards.

What to Expect:

  • Fast-paced, high-energy environment. You’ll be on your feet, moving quickly, and handling a steady flow of customers for up to 10-hour shifts!

Up to $16.50 per hour

title: Software Engineer (.NET/AI)
description:
• AI Scale up in the legal tech space!
  • Build on a genuinely greenfield platform – you're shaping the foundations, not patching someone else's
  • Flexible, hybrid Sydney based role - 2 days a week in the office


About Corto


We are CORTO, a cutting-edge software company dedicated to revolutionising the legal industry. Our mission is to empower legal practitioners with AI-driven solutions that streamline their workflow, boost productivity, and provide more efficient client service.

Our team of AI experts and engineers collaborate to develop intelligent software tailored to the unique needs of lawyers, paralegals, and legal assistants. Our innovative AI solutions automate routine tasks, simplify document management, and enhance decision-making, allowing legal professionals to focus on what they do best - providing expert legal counsel.

We're rapidly scaling from 80 to 250+ employees, with a highly technical workforce where around 75% of the team are developers and engineers. Working alongside our Sydney-based team of passionate high achievers, you'll join a fast-growing technology business where things rarely stay the same for long - and if you're smart, caring, and ambitious, you'll be in great company.

What you'll do

We are looking for an experienced Software Engineer to join our AI Platform team at a mid-to-senior level. You'll be working on a largely greenfield codebase, designing, building, testing and maintaining scalable APIs and backend services, with a strong focus on shaping and testing the AI capabilities already built into our platform.

To make this happen, you will:

  • Develop and maintain backend services using C# and .NET
  • Design and evolve scalable APIs for internal and external consumers
  • Integrate AI-powered capabilities into existing systems
  • Work with AWS services to build and deploy cloud-based solutions
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to deliver clean, effective solutions
  • Contribute to code reviews and engineering best practices
  • Continuously improve systems, processes, and code quality

What you’ll bring

You are an experienced developer who takes ownership and delivers high-quality solutions. In addition to that you will bring:

  • Strong experience with .NET / C# (5+ years)
  • Experience building RESTful APIs (ASP.NET Web API) used by multiple consumers
  • Solid understanding of SOLID principles and clean architecture
  • Hands-on experience with AWS or other cloud platforms
  • Experience using AI-assisted dev tools to design, write, test and review software
  • Ability to critically evaluate AI-generated code for correctness, security, performance, and maintainability
  • Experience applying prompt and context-engineering techniques to improve software-development outcomes

Even better if you have:

  • Experience building or integrating MCP servers, clients, or tools
  • Experience designing scalable systems and identifying and resolving performance bottlenecks

You are the type of person who:

  • Takes ownership and delivers end-to-end
  • Communicates clearly and collaborates effectively
  • Solves problems with a practical, solution-focused mindset
  • Is comfortable working in a fast-paced environment
  • Continuously looks to improve systems and ways of working
  • Maintains a positive and pragmatic attitude

Why join CORTO?

  • Your work matters. We solve real world problems that improve and support local, everyday law firms. So they can do their best work for the people in the communities they serve.
  • Make an impact. You won't be another 'cog in the wheel' here. We give full trust and autonomy for you to be heard, to work on big & complex projects - and to make a real difference.
  • Work with a group of authentic, passionate people who love what they do.
  • Well-funded and global. CORTO is part of ATI - one of the largest international LegalTech companies.
  • Flexible and hybrid working. We engage, share, and collaborate on ideas and workflows.
  • Career and learning opportunities; we move fast and need smart people to get us where we're going. We are a scaling business and looking for people who want to grow with us.
  • Have fun with us. Celebrations. Socials. Sports teams. Access to sailing and yacht events.
  • We value your well-being - Wellness focus with additional time off, gym membership and other perks.
  • Fast-paced tech environment, if we don't disrupt ourselves someone else will do it!
  • Access to LEAP Home - a program unique to us to support you in buying your primary residence.

title: Senior Network and Security Engineer
description:
ABOUT TEMENOS


Temenos is a global leader in banking technology. Through our market-leading core banking suite and best-in-class composable solutions, we are modernizing the banking industry. Banks of all sizes utilize our adaptable technology – on-premises, in the cloud, or as SaaS – to deliver next-generation services and AI-enhanced experiences that elevate banking for their customers. VALUES


Care about transforming the Banking landscape.

Commit to being part of an exciting culture and product evolving within the financial industry.

Collaborate effectively and proactively with teams within or outside Temenos.

Challenge yourself to be ambitious and achieve your individual as well as the company targets.


Do you want to dive deeper into the world of complex networks? In the Network and Security Operations Department, you will support the smooth operation of all network services for our customers and Temenos AG. As part of the Network and Security Operations team, you will work within an exciting and evolving environment ranging from classic LAN core services and WAN infrastructure to modern cloud networking setups. Take the opportunity to become a network engineer in a transforming network landscape at Temenos.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • You will troubleshoot network and security issues and plan, implement, and document changes in accordance with established processes, SLAs, and ITIL standards.

  • You will proactively optimize network environments by migrating, updating, monitoring, and adjusting systems as part of a major network refresh and transformation program.

  • You will operate, configure, and maintain network and security solutions using technologies such as Cisco Meraki, Fortinet, and Arista.

  • You will contribute to the introduction and expansion of automation using Ansible and GitLab, leveraging platform APIs to improve efficiency.

  • You will support and actively drive the transition toward Infrastructure as Code within network operations.

  • You will participate in on-call duty as well as planned off-hour changes in alignment with service level agreements.

  • You will collaborate with team members to ensure stable, secure, and scalable network services across all environments.

SKILLS

  • You should have hands-on experience in operating enterprise networks, including routing and switching.

  • You should have strong troubleshooting skills and routine experience working with network devices via the CLI.

  • You should have the ability to orient yourself quickly within complex network environments.

  • You should have basic knowledge of Linux systems.

  • You should have completed formal training or studies in the IT or network field or possess equivalent practical experience as a career changer.

  • You should have good knowledge of Cisco Meraki and Fortinet technologies, with Arista experience considered a strong plus.

  • You should have a self-driven mindset with a strong desire for continuous learning, supported by learning platforms and training opportunities.

  • You should have a high degree of independence, initiative, and personal responsibility in your daily work.

  • You should have a collaborative team mindset and appreciate an open error culture focused on learning and continuous improvement.

  • You should have very good written and spoken English skills, with additional languages considered a plus.

  • You should have vendor certifications such as CCNP, FCP, or equivalent, which are considered an advantage.

  • You should have the willingness and ability to travel when required


SOME OF OUR BENEFITS include:

  • Maternity leave: Transition back with 3 days per week in the first month and 4 days per week in the second month

  • Civil Partnership: 1 week of paid leave if you're getting married. This covers marriages and civil partnerships, including same sex/civil partnership

  • Family care: 4 weeks of paid family care leave

  • Recharge days: 4 days per year to use when you need to physically or mentally needed to recharge

  • Study leaves: 2 weeks of paid leave each year for study or personal development

title: Senior Software Engineer, State Estimation
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

At Anduril, our Software Engineers specialize in solving complex, real-world problems through cutting-edge algorithms and intelligent software integrations. Operating in small, innovative teams, we push the boundaries of what's possible to deliver advanced technologies with mission-critical applications. Our commitment doesn't end with academic research or proof-of-concept experiments; we measure our success by the real-world impact of our deployed solutions. Inspired by Arthur C. Clarke’s vision — “Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic” — we aim to achieve groundbreaking results in target tracking, state estimation, and situational awareness. We are currently seeking highly talented technologists to join our mission and redefine the future of defense technology.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

  • Define and influence the direction of a small team, leveraging your subject-matter expertise in target tracking and state estimation.
  • Prototype and deploy state-of-the-art algorithms for tracking, multi-sensor data fusion, and state estimation in agile, iterative development environments.
  • Develop high-performance software for real-time systems, ranging from tactical implementations to simulation environments and decision support tools.
  • Design and implement robust filters, estimators, and probabilistic reasoning systems that enable actionable insights from noisy, ambiguous, or incomplete sensor data.
  • Analyze system performance using high-fidelity simulations, innovative modeling tools, and rigorous statistical techniques to validate the benefits of our technology.
  • Drive customer success by customizing algorithms and software for mission-critical use cases, including real-time tracking and sensor fusion.
  • Integrate tracking and estimation technologies into the broader software development lifecycle, from requirements definition through testing and optimization.
  • Translate technical progress into clear, actionable insights for diverse stakeholders, including colleagues and end-users.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8+ years of experience in algorithm design, software development, and statistical modeling with programming expertise in C/C++, Python, and Matlab.
  • Strong knowledge of target tracking techniques, such as Kalman filters, particle filters, and multi-target tracking algorithms (e.g., JPDA, MHT, or PHD filters).
  • Experience in state estimation, including Bayesian filtering, sensor fusion, and recursive estimation techniques.
  • Solid understanding of applied mathematics, including linear algebra, optimization, probability, and stochastic processes.
  • Knowledge of signal processing techniques for interpreting diverse sensor data (e.g., radar, lidar, EO/IR).
  • Familiarity with big data pipelines, NoSQL databases, and the efficient handling of large-scale sensor data.
  • Background in machine learning as applied to target tracking and recognition, including clustering, classification, and anomaly detection techniques.
  • Ability to engineer robust systems for estimation theory, adaptive filtering, controls, and complex signal environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to work across development lifecycles, from prototyping to optimizing production systems.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance.

We request transcripts as part of the early application process to understand your academic background and how your coursework supports the skills deemed critical for the role. Transcripts help us assess your technical and analytical abilities, complementing our interview process in which we also evaluate practical experience and cultural fit. If you choose not to share your transcripts, you will need to provide detailed information regarding your academic performance in relevant courses, including projects and coursework specifics, to ensure we evaluate your academic accomplishments properly. If you do provide academic transcripts, feel free to redact non-technical information (e.g., student ID, dates, non-technical coursework, etc.). Unofficial transcripts obtained online acceptable for this assessment.

US Salary Range
$190,000—$252,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

  • No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

  • Please always verify communications:
    • Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
    • Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

  • Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

  • What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit .

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Computer Vision and Autonomy Lead
description:
Charles River Analytics, a GRVTY company, creates solutions and technology to tackle the world’s most challenging problems. Our team of technological entrepreneurs works together to push at the forefront of enhanced AI, robotics, smart sensing, and human-centered computing. The resulting research and development help to continuously advance government programs and discover new possibilities in the commercial marketplace. At Charles River, we take great pride in our success at attracting and retaining the most talented and creative problem-solvers in our field. Now a part of GRVTY, we offer the same trusted capabilities with increased organizational depth and expanded capacity across mission-critical national security domains. Are you ready to accelerate our mission-focused innovations? We’d love to hear from you!

We are seeking a Senior Software Engineering Leader to provide technical leadership, architectural guidance, and team management for projects involving robotic navigation, autonomous systems, and advanced sensor processing. This position includes both senior-level technical responsibilities and the future opportunity to lead a team of engineers. The ideal candidate demonstrates deep expertise in computer vision and autonomy, strong communication skills, and an interest in developing and mentoring engineering staff.

How you will make an impact:

  • Provide technical leadership in the design, development, and integration of our existing computer vision and autonomy algorithms and software systems.
  • Lead and mentor a team of computer vision, perception, and autonomy engineers; support hiring, onboarding, performance feedback, time management, and professional development.
  • Develop robust, maintainable software solutions for applications such as object detection and tracking, SLAM, visual odometry, sensor fusion, and image processing.
  • Optimize and deploy machine learning models on embedded, edge, and real-time systems using frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.
  • Oversee system architecture, technical reviews, code quality, and adherence to engineering best practices.
  • Collaborate with scientists, engineers, and operational subject matter experts to define technical requirements and translate research concepts into implementable solutions serving the ground, sea, air and space domains.
  • Participate in customer engagements, including technical briefings, requirements discussions, field testing, and integration activities.
  • Contribute to proposal development, technical documentation, reports, and transition planning for applied research and product development programs.
  • Support the growth and scaling of internal technical capabilities to meet emerging program and commercialization needs.

What you need:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field; a master’s degree or equivalent experience is preferred.
  • 10 or more years of experience (or a master’s degree with 8 or more years) in computer vision, perception, or autonomy system development.
  • Proficiency in Python and C++ with experience developing both research prototypes and production quality software.
  • Experience working with robotics frameworks such as ROS2 and simulation environments.
  • Demonstrated expertise in several key areas of computer vision, including object detection, tracking, SLAM, visual odometry, segmentation, or related fields.
  • Experience conducting laboratory and field testing of robotic or autonomous systems.
  • Familiarity with networking, system integration, and distributed system debugging.
  • Strong understanding of software development best practices, including testing, version control, and code review processes.
  • Demonstrated interest in technical team leadership and the ability to support the development of engineering talent.
  • Ability and willingness to travel for customer meetings, integration events, and field exercises.
  • U.S. Citizenship.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government Security Clearance.
  • Ability to work on a hybrid schedule with at least 60% in-office presence at our Cambridge headquarters.

Our ideal candidate has:

  • Experience with systems engineering, requirements analysis, and system level design.
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines or modern DevOps/DevSecOps methodologies.
  • Experience with containerization (Docker) and orchestration (Kubernetes, Helm)
  • Experience integrating complex software systems into larger systems (APIs, communication).
  • Familiarity with tools such as OpenCV, PyTorch, TensorFlow, and CUDA.
  • Experience with data engineering practices and management of large datasets.
  • Experience preparing technical deliverables such as specifications, reports, or contributions to academic publications.

Salary Range

$175,000 - $225,000

The above salary range is an estimate based on the internal job level(s) for which this role is being considered. The final salary will be decided after careful evaluation of the individual's work experience, education, and overall qualifications. This range does not include the substantial total rewards, as listed below, that you will also be eligible for as an employee at Charles River Analytics.

Why Charles River?

Charles River Analytics thrives on collaboration and values each team member. We offer competitive compensation plus bonus and retirement contribution, with an attractive benefits package including 100% employer-paid medical and dental insurance, as well as vision, life, and disability insurance, paid maternity/paternity leave, tuition reimbursement, monthly gym allowance, free parking, generous paid time off, and a casual environment. We offer tremendous flexibility and value work-life balance. We are also accessible by public transportation. Charles River became an employee-owned company in 2012, to set the stage for the next-generation of innovation, service, and growth in R&D. As we entered 2026, we joined forces with GRVTY, gaining the scale and capacity to transition, field, and sustain our innovations faster and more effectively than ever before.

title: Davies Lab Scientist I or II
description:

Regular

Job Profile:

Scientist I

Job Summary:

This position is focused on clinical and translational cancer research rather than basic science laboratory research. While the position supports research studies and clinical trials, it does not involve bench science, laboratory experimentation, or routine operation of scientific laboratory equipment. Training in mixed methods techniques as applied to clinical trial recruitment will be provided. The successful candidate will work closely with multidisciplinary research teams, patients, and study sites to support recruitment, implementation, and development of clinical research studies.

  • This position may require some work to be performed in-person, onsite, at a designated campus work location. Some work may be performed remotely, at an offsite, non-campus work location.

  • This position has been identified as a position of trust with access to vulnerable populations. The selected candidate will be required to pass an initial caregiver check to be eligible for employment under the Wisconsin Caregiver Law and every four years.

  • Applicants for this position will be considered for the following titles: Scientist I and Scientist II. The title is determined by the experience and qualifications of the finalist.

  • This vacancy is being announced simultaneously with JR#10011794; please note that only one vacancy exists. Having two job postings allows the department of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery to consider candidates with both Scientist and Researcher qualifications for this position.

Key Job Responsibilities:

  • Collects and analyzes research data, conducts experiments and interviews, and documents results according to established policies and procedures under general supervision and limited responsibility
  • Assists with the identification of research problems and the development of research methodologies and procedures
  • Serves as a main point of contact and liaison with internal and external stakeholders providing information and representing the interests of a specialized research area
  • Attends and assists with the facilitation of scholarly events and presentations in support of continued professional development and the dissemination of research information
  • Conducts literature reviews, prepares reports and materials, and disseminates information to appropriate entities
  • Writes or assists in developing grant applications and proposals to secure research funding

Department:

School of Medicine and Public Health, Department of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, Davies Lab

In 1930, Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery (Oto-HNS) was added as a division within the University of Wisconsin Department of Surgery. In 2025, after decades of growth and achievement, the division became an independent department within the School of Medicine and Public Health. Oto-HNS includes seven divisions: otology and neurotology, laryngology, pediatric otolaryngology, comprehensive otolaryngology, rhinology and skull base surgery, head and neck oncologic surgery, and facial plastic and reconstructive surgery. We provide a full range of state-of-the-art specialized care for adults and children at six clinical practice sites in the Madison area, and six outreach sites across Wisconsin and Illinois. Our team of nationally and internationally renowned faculty and residents prioritizes a collaborative culture, engaging with specialists across our practice sites and throughout campus. The department offers the highest quality of education to a large variety of learners, providing training to well over 100 individuals each year through clinical rotations, extramurally funded traineeships, externships and more.

The starting salary for this position is $70,000, but is negotiable based on experience and qualifications.

Employees in this position can expect to receive benefits such as generous vacation, holidays, and sick leave; competitive insurances and savings accounts; retirement benefits. For more information, refer to the campus benefits webpage.

Caitlin Spaulding, staley@wisc.edu, 608-265-1325

Diversity is a source of strength, creativity, and innovation for UW-Madison. title: Factory Planner
description:
About IonQ:

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.

Location: This role will work onsite at our office located in Bothell, WA.
Travel: Minimal
Job ID: 1844

The Role:

We are looking for a Factory Planner to join our Supply Chain team. As a Factory Planner, you'll be part of a cross-functional team whose mission is to lead IonQ on its journey to build the world's best quantum computers to solve the world's most complex problems.

In this role, you will own the production schedule that connects demand to the shop floor — translating forecast and firm demand into executable build plans, releasing and maintaining work orders in the ERP, and driving material availability so that manufacturing has the right parts, in the right quantity, at the right time.

This is a hands-on planning role in a high-mix, evolving manufacturing environment. Engineering changes are frequent, lead times are long, and the build plan shifts as priorities change. The ideal candidate is someone who is disciplined about data hygiene in the ERP, communicates clearly with production and procurement, and has the judgment to know which fires actually need putting out.

Responsibilities:

Production Planning & Scheduling

  • Build and maintain the production schedule based on demand signals, capacity constraints, and material availability
  • Create, release, and close work orders in NetSuite; maintain accurate start dates, due dates, and quantities
  • Level-load the schedule against labor, tooling, and workcenter capacity; identify and escalate bottlenecks before they impact delivery
  • Sequence builds to balance on-time delivery against WIP, changeover, and resource efficiency

Material Planning

  • Run and action MRP output: release planned orders, reschedule in/out, and resolve exception messages
  • Partner with Buyer Planners on shortages, expedites, and long-lead-time commitments
  • Maintain planning parameters — lead times, safety stock, reorder points, lot sizing, planning time fences — and review them for accuracy on a regular cadence
  • Track and communicate a clear, prioritized shortage list to the production and procurement teams

Execution & Cross-Functional Support

  • Lead or participate in daily production meetings; report schedule status, risks, and recovery plans
  • Work with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality to resolve BOM, routing, and yield issues that affect the plan
  • Support engineering change implementation: assess inventory and WIP impact, plan cut-in points, and manage disposition of obsolete material
  • Coordinate kitting and material staging with Warehouse/Stockroom to keep builds moving

Data Integrity & Continuous Improvement

  • Maintain accurate item master, BOM, and routing data within the ERP; drive correction of errors at the source
  • Reconcile inventory discrepancies affecting plan accuracy and partner with Inventory Control on root cause
  • Report on planning KPIs: schedule attainment, on-time delivery, inventory turns, shortage count, past-due work orders
  • Identify and implement process improvements; document workflows so the process survives turnover

Requirements:

  • 3+ years of production planning, master scheduling, or materials planning experience in a manufacturing environment, or an equivalent combination of education and experience
  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Industrial Engineering, Business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • Working knowledge of MRP/ERP systems and the logic behind them (planned orders, pegging, exception messages, planning parameters)
  • Strong Excel skills — pivot tables, lookups, and the ability to build a working analysis without waiting on a report request
  • Demonstrated ability to read and interpret BOMs, routings, and engineering drawings
  • Clear written and verbal communication; comfortable pushing back on unrealistic requests with data

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with NetSuite or a comparable Tier 1/Tier 2 ERP
  • Background in high-mix / low-volume, prototype-to-production, or new product introduction environments
  • APICS/ASCM certification (CPIM, CSCP) or active pursuit
  • Familiarity with lean manufacturing, kanban, or pull-based replenishment
  • Experience supporting engineering change orders and revision-controlled builds
  • Working knowledge of business intelligence reporting tools

The total compensation package includes base, bonus, equity, and a range of benefit options found on our career site.

If this role has a commission structure, the compensation range below just reflects the base compensation range.

$80,000—$120,000 USD

description:
Current Employees: If you are currently employed at any of the Universities of Wisconsin, log in to Workday to apply through the internal application process.

Research Specialist

Job Summary:

The Wisconsin Crop Innovation Center (WCIC) at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is seeking a highly motivated, independent, and detail-oriented individual to join the Plant Analysis Team as a Research Specialist.

Join WCIC’s Plant Analysis Team and help confirm the success of cutting-edge plant transformation projects. As a Plant Analysis Research Specialist, you will work under moderate supervision and test hundreds of plants each week using molecular techniques such as PCR, qPCR, ddPCR, and PACE—and communicate results that guide greenhouse decisions and project direction. You will sample plants, extract DNA, perform genetic assays, interpret sequence data, maintain laboratory supplies, and work alongside student employees. This position also offers opportunities to expand your skills in plant transformation, plasmid construction, and transgenic plant greenhouse management.

WCIC is a ~100,000 square foot state-of-the-art agricultural biotechnology complex, housing laboratories and greenhouses dedicated to the production and analysis of transgenic and gene edited plants. This facility is the largest publicly held plant transformation facility in the United States and is aimed at improving crop plants for humans, livestock, and the environment.

Key Job Responsibilities:

  • Reviews, analyzes, and interprets data and/or documents results for presentations and/or reporting to internal and external audiences
  • Performs literature reviews and writes reports
  • Conducts research experiments according to established research protocols with moderate impact to the project(s). Collects data and monitors test results
  • Participates in the development, interpretation, and implementation of research methodology and materials
  • Operates, cleans, and maintains organization of research equipment and research area. Tracks inventory levels and places replenishment orders
  • Provides operational guidance on day-to-day activities of unit or program staff and/or student workers

The Wisconsin Crop Innovation Center (WCIC)

  • Minimum of 1 year of laboratory experience in academic, industry, or research settings (may include undergraduate research experience)

  • Minimum of 1 year of experience with standard molecular biology techniques (for example pipetting, DNA extraction, PCR, Gel Electrophoresis)

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in advanced molecular biology techniques (multi-channel pipetting, automated pipetting, RNA extraction, qPCR, ddPCR, PACE / KASP assays, primer and probe design)

  • Hands on experience with plants / greenhouse
