title: Intake Specialist
description:
Job Title: Intake Specialist

Job Location: Brentwood/Goodlettsville, TN

Job Shift: Full Time

We are looking for an Intake Specialist to join our Home Health team. Come make a difference in the Brentwood/Goodlettsville, TN area and surrounding communities! At Beacon Home Health, our employees enjoy:

  • Opportunities to build trusted relationships and connections while providing care to patients.

  • To be valued and respected by patients and their families.

  • A sense of security, incredible team support, and flexibility for work-life balance.

  • Leadership development opportunities – we value internal advancement in areas of interest to our employees.

POSITION SUMMARY: The Intake Coordinator is responsible for performing all steps of the patient intake and referral process. This role is essential for ensuring that every patient referred to the agency is accurately vetted, documented, and approved for services in a timely manner.


ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES INCLUDE BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO THE FOLLOWING:
• Serves as the primary contact for referral reception from hospitals, physician offices, and other sources, accurately gathering all necessary demographic and clinical information.
• Creates the patient shell and initial patient record within the Homecare Homebase (HCHB) EMR system.
• Performs thorough checking of patient eligibility for home health or hospice services against regulatory and payer criteria, ensuring the patient meets the requirements for home health or hospice.
• Conducts comprehensive insurance verification and benefit checks for all potential patients to confirm coverage and benefits.
• Initiates and tracks the requesting of initial insurance authorization for services, communicating with payers until approval is secured.
• Communicates effectively with clinical teams, referral sources, and physicians to obtain missing documentation and clarify patient needs or service eligibility.
• Ensures all aspects of the intake process are compliant with federal, state, and payer rules and are completed within required timeframes.
• Other appropriate services and special projects as assigned.

The above statements are only meant to be a representative summary of the major duties and responsibilities performed by incumbents of this job. The incumbents may be requested to perform job-related tasks other than those stated in this description.

QUALIFICATIONS & REQUIREMENTS FOR THE POSITION:
• At least one (1) year of experience in a healthcare office setting, such as admissions, patient access, or intake, with experience in home health or hospice preferred.
• Demonstrated experience or ability to quickly learn and utilize an Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system; familiarity with Homecare Homebase (HCHB) is a major plus.
• Basic knowledge of Medicare, Medicaid and commercial insurance plans and terminology related to eligibility and authorization.
• Strong understanding of medical terminology and documentation requirements.

PREFERRED KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS:
• Excellent time management and organization skills.
• Strong problem-solving skills to resolve insurance and documentation issues.
• Ability to work effectively in a high-volume, fast-paced environment and prioritize multiple tasks.
• Exceptional attention to detail.
• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex cases simultaneously.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills with a professional telephone demeanor.
• Compassionate and empathetic approach to patient and family interactions.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
• Job may require heavy use of office equipment, including computer, tablet, and phone.
• Must have the reasonable ability to stand, walk, sit, use hands to finger, handle, feel, reach, balance, see, talk, hear, and drive. Must be reasonably capable of lifting over twenty (20) pounds.
• Minimal portion (<30%) of daily assignments may require travel to client/resident/patient locations or other work sites, via car or public transportation.
• Work schedule may occasionally require evening, night, holiday, or weekend assignments.

The employer for this position is stated in the job posting. The Pennant Group, Inc. is a holding company of independent operating subsidiaries that provide healthcare services through home health and hospice agencies and senior living communities located throughout the US. Each of these businesses is operated by a separate, independent operating subsidiary that has its own management, employees and assets. More information about The Pennant Group, Inc. is available at http://www.pennantgroup.com.

Job Summary:

Care Partners are responsible for meeting the basic needs of patients by providing skilled levels of bedside patient care under the direction of the Registered Nurse. Care Partners also perform clerical duties necessary to the functioning of the nursing unit.

Job Responsibilities and Requirements:

POSITION ACCOUNTABILITIES AND PERFORMANCE CRITERIA (% of Time)

Essential Functions: The following are essential job accountabilities and performance criteria:

1) General Patient Care:

Criteria

A) Carries out the patient’s plan of care as it relates to the patient’s physical needs under the direction of the Registered Nurse.

B) Delivers care requiring broad knowledge of aseptic technique, medical terminology and equipment.

C) Assists nurses and physicians with procedures.

D) Maintains knowledge of and operates equipment used in patient care safely.

E) Retrieves patient care items that are not routinely available on the unit.

F) Retrieves, recovers or follows up on patient care needs.

G) Completed unit clerical duties including the coordination of designated unit activities, transcription of orders, medical record maintenance and serving as a unit receptionist.

H) Prepares rooms prior to admissions and following discharges. Completes patient’s belongings list on admission and transfer.

I) Directs prompt and courteous attention to the needs of patients, families, and visitors.

J) Rounds with purpose.

K) Engages in service recovery activities referring unusual problems to Nurse Manager/ Designate.

L) Rounds after dietary trays are passed to ensure all meals are appropriate or as required for patient satisfaction /care needs.

M) Takes appropriate action when necessary including the resolution of issues related to late or wrong trays.

N) Feeds and sets up trays as needed.

O) Recognizes needs and initiates appropriate action in regard to maintaining supplies and equipment

P) Notifies appropriate department in order to maintain a clean safe environment (housekeeping, maintenance, dietary, etc.)

Q) Functions as a resource person to co-workers, patients/families, medical staff, and ancillary personnel.

2) Safety and Comfort

Criteria

A) Correctly places restraints; observes for constriction of circulation, changes to skin integrity, adequate breathing; knows when and how to change position; provides range of motion (ROM) and skin care, toileting, and opportunities for socialization.

B) Operates Cardiac Monitor i.e.

1. On/off switch

2. Alarms/stand-by

3. Obtaining strip

4. Lead placement

3) Vital Signs/Measurement

Criteria

A) Completes Point of Care Testing as approved by hospital and competency

B) Obtains vital signs including temperature

C) Measures abdominal girth

D) Weighs patients

E) Measures intake and output

4) Mobility and Exercise:

Criteria

A) Applies Pneumatic Air Stockings / Ted Hose

B) Ambulates, turns and positions patients.

5) Respiratory Care

Criteria

A) Assists with incentive spirometry and cough / deep breath.

B) Sets up oxygen therapy such as, nasal cannula or mask as directed by Registered Nurse.

C) Monitors pulse oximetry

D) Completes tracheostomy care

E) Performs suctioning

1. Oral

2. Tracheal: When the patient is assessed by the Registered Nurse to be stable.

6) Wound Care

Criteria

A) Places patient on specialty bed

B) Performs dressing changes (sterile and clean)

C) Cares for pin care site after assessment has been completed by the Registered Nurse. Assists in monitoring that traction weights are hanging freely and in good alignment.

7) Bowel and Bladder Elimination

Criteria

A) Administers enemas

B) Performs straight catheterization. Provides catheter care.

8) Hygiene

Criteria

A) Provides:

1. Hygiene and grooming daily

2. Mouth care (including dentures) at least twice/day.

3. Fresh water at 0800, 1600, 2400 and as needed

4. Perineal care

5. Toileting

9) Specimen Collection

Criteria

A) Obtains:

1. Midstream (clean-voided) urine specimen.

2. Timed urine specimen

3. Sterile urine specimen from an indwelling catheter

4. Urine specific gravity (5 South and 5 ICU only)

5. Urine pH

6. Expectorated sputum specimens

7. Blood specimens by venipuncture

8. Stool specimens

10) Clerical

Criteria

A) Answers phone within 3 rings identifying self, title and nursing unit. Does not keep person on hold for extended periods.

B) Provides directions to physicians, hospital personnel, and visitors to patient’s room.

C) Notifies the physician and nursing staff of new patient’s arrival to unit.

D) Assists in the receiving of articles brought to the nursing unit.

E) Answers pneumatic tube promptly and returns carriers to the appropriate area.

F) Prepares a daily worksheet and confirms all appointments concerning daily work (including blood work) and updates worksheet on each shift.

G) Verifies census sheet, maintains and updates as necessary.

H) Informs Admitting Department of all transfers, discharges, admissions, room changes, and deaths through the computer. Includes disposition of appropriate paperwork.

I) Informs staff/charge nurses / nurse manager of nursing unit activities: return of patients to the floor, physician stat orders, new admissions, etc.

J) Assist nursing staff and ancillary personnel to ensure appropriate and complete specimen labels/requisition orders.

K) Reports critical lab values to appropriate personnel.

L) Initiates and completes secretarial portion of the pre-op checklist.

M) Completes the administrative data screen for all new admissions and updates daily.

N) Assists the nursing staff with paperwork involved in the patient transfer and discharge procedure to include movement of medications.

O) Gives a full report to the oncoming person. (Leaves a written report if unable to give verbal). Informs the Charge Nurse if additional orders are left for the night shift.

P) Checks patient chart periodically throughout the shift for “stat”, flagged and un-flagged orders.

Q) Checks physician orders daily for unsigned verbal/telephone orders and places appropriate flag.

R) Enters orders into the computer accurately.

S) Calls departments to order tests, procedures, and consults which cannot be ordered through the computer.

T) Transcribes orders for tests/procedures/consults onto the TESTS/PROCEDURES section of the profile.

U) Ensures labels are correctly placed on all forms

V) Transcribes medication orders to the medication administration record accurately.

W) Places all physician orders in pharmacy bin. Faxes all physician orders to pharmacy during night shift.

X) Signs orders to indicate orders were taken off with date, time, signature and title

Y) Utilizes appropriate backup systems in the event of computer downtime.

Z) Ensures that stat and timed orders are transcribed promptly.

AA) Initiates and assembles charts

BB) Keeps chart in order; thins chart as needed and places in appropriate file.

CC) Obtains old charges from Medical Records through the computer.

DD) Ensures that Medical Records picks up old charts by placing them in assigned pick up area on day of discharge.

EE) Completes medical record checklist and ensures that the complete chart is sent to Medical Records within 24 hours of discharge and immediately upon patient death.

FF) Sends complete chart including thinned chart and old chart on transfer to patient.

GG) Ensures allergy, and isolation cards are posted in charts when indicated.

HH) Completes and signs secretarial portion of death summary.

11) Safety/Infection Control: Performs job in accordance with safety and infection control policies. (5,8) 5%

Criteria

A) Practices standard precautions and disposes of hazardous wastes per established guidelines.

B) Maintains a safe, clean, comfortable, and therapeutic environment for patients / families / employees in accordance to hospital standards.

1. Maintains clutter free environment.

2. Keeps personal conversations/background noise to a minimum.

3. Adheres to dress code.

C) Reports risk management concerns.

D) Assumes responsibility for completing all annual mandatory requirements:

1. Yearly TB Screening

2. Annual Ethics Training (Initial Ethics, if new employee)

3. Annual Safety Training

4. Required Information Security course

5. Required Abuse & Neglect course

6. Annual Blood Borne Pathogens training (if required)

7. Coursework as assigned for .edu

8. Annual competency

9. Age/Population specific competency (if applicable)

10. Orientation competency (if new hire)

11. Unit Specific

E) Obtains report from Registered Nurse and informs nurse of changes in patient’s condition.

F) Communicates concerns or patient complaints to Registered Nurse and other team members as appropriate.

G) Documents all procedures and care concisely and legibly on chart forms according to chart form guidelines.

H) Identifies problems, gathers pertinent data, suggests solutions, communicates using appropriate lines of authority, and works toward problem resolution.

I) Empties soiled linen containers.

J) Works in a constant state of alertness and safe manner.

12) Service: Provides service excellence to the customers of Saint Louis University Hospital by delivering timely, high quality care in a courteous, and respectful manner. (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) 10%

Criteria

A) Demonstrates care and courtesy

1. Provides prompt, respectful, courteous service.

2.Meets physical, spiritual, psychological and emotional needs of patients and families as directed by Registered Nurse.

3. Responds to call lights promptly.

4. Apologizes for mix-up and delay.

B) Communicates effectively and maintains confidentiality

1. Listens to staff/patient / family concerns and addresses needs within scope of responsibility.

2. Explains procedures and all education in a manner that staff / patient/ family understands.

3. Allows time for questions.

C) Demonstrates competence and collaboration

1. Provides accurate change of shift report.

2. Provides quality care in accordance to standards.

3. Shares knowledge with other departments to facilitate work flow and continuity.

D) Provides cost effect services

1. Uses resources wisely.

2. Recommends changes in practice that increases efficiency and minimizes waste.

13) Personal Accountability: Demonstrates accountability for own job performance. (6) 5%

Criteria

A) Adheres to and incorporates all customer service standards in patient care and work practices.

B) Participates in additional learning experiences to increase competence including:

1. Staff meetings

2. Mandatory in-services and educational programs

3. Evaluation of self-performance by identifying strengths and areas for improvement.

C) Assists in identifying and implementing nursing unit goals.

14) Performance Improvement (PI): Incorporates Performance Improvement into one's job performance. (6) 5%

Criteria

A) Identifies problems, participation in data collection when requested, suggests solutions, communicates using appropriate lines of authority and works toward problem resolution.

B) Participates in the performance / process improvement process.

1. Assists in developing unit based PI plan.

2. Participates in discussion of PI outcomes.

3. Collaborates in developing and implementing action plans.

C) Incorporates Performance Improvement and Commitment to Quality (C2Q) results into job performance

D) Offers suggestions for improvement of unit activities.

E) Participates in discussion of PI C2Q data outcomes.

F) Collects PI C2Q data as assigned

G) Participates in research activities on the nursing unit as appropriate.

15) Age Appropriate Care: Provides age-appropriate care to:

____Infant ___Child ____Adolescent _____Adult _____Geriatric

Criteria

A) Demonstrates knowledge and skills of normal growth & development necessary to provide services to the age of the patient served by the department.

B) Demonstrates ability to assess and interpret age specific data to identify patient needs.

C) Utilizes communication skills necessary to interpret age specific responses to service and interaction.

D) Involves family or significant other in decision making related to services provided.

E) Demonstrates ability to provide service needed for the age groups routinely served by the department assigned.

F) Position specific: Need to enter those responsibilities specific for position

16) Specialized Care: Provides specialized care to patients at high risk for injury.

(1, 2, 4, 5, 8) <1%

Criteria

A) Restraint Care

1. Initiates/evaluates alternatives to restraint prior to application.

2. Applies restraints consistent with the approved procedure.

3. Monitors and assesses patient’s response throughout the restraint period at the appropriate intervals.

4. Provides specified patient care (toileting, skin care, hydration, feeding, etc.) on a timely basis.

5. Provides for trail release and removal of restraint as soon as possible.

B) Pain Management

1. Follows pain management plan of care, e.g.: repositioning, message, immobilization, music therapy etc.

2. Reports patient complaints of pain to the nursing staff and/or physician.

C) Abuse Assessment

1. Is aware of abuse recognition criteria and incorporates it into assessments.

2. Reports signs of possible abuse/neglect to the physician & Risk Management, and recommends appropriate consultations (psychiatric, Social Work) for evaluation.

DISCLAIMER: Performs other related duties as assigned or requested.

Rationale for Essential Functions:

1) The performance of this function is the reason the job exists.

2) There are limited employees among whom the performance of this function can be distributed.

3) This function occupies a great deal of the employee’s time.

4) This function is highly specialized. Employees are hired for the skill/ability to perform this function.

5) Failure to perform this function may have serious consequences.

6) The function was performed by past employees, and is performed by current employees.

Standard (I understand that…)

Own and Respect My Environment By:

Standard (I understand that…)

Treating my colleagues, our patients, visitors, and business partners with respect and dignity is necessary to create an environment where excellence in caring and nursing practice can thrive. (People)

Expectations (So I will…)

  • Show empathy to every patient and communicate my commitment to assist in their comfort, safety, and restoration to health.

  • Offer constructive criticism to co-workers when addressing concerns, praising in public and criticizing in private when necessary.
  • Be part of the solution – not part of the problem.
  • Not complain to or complain in front of my patients/families and staff (i.e. too busy or short staffed, no lunch).

  • Respond promptly to patient requests.

Standard (I understand that…)

Patients and their families are scared and vulnerable. It is my responsibility to communicate through verbal and non-vernal means that I am here to help. (Service)

Expectations (So I will…)

  • Introduce myself to all my patients and family members.
  • Take time to tell them what to expect and keep them informed.
  • Answer lights promptly to meet a patient’s needs and prevent patient falls.
  • Respect the patient’s privacy and modesty – close curtains, cover patient, reduce traffic in patient’s room during procedures.
  • Explain all procedures, test, medications and monitoring equipment, etc to each patient and discuss plan of care for the day/shift with patient and family.
  • Be compassionate and empathetic to their concerns at all times.

The intent of this agreement is not to provide a complete list of job responsibilities. Its intent rather is to be a positive statement of concrete actions which will ensure that nursing practice at Saint Louis University Hospital sets the benchmark for excellence in service, quality, and people.

As a member of the nursing staff at Saint Louis University Hospital, I understand that on behalf of my hospital, our patients and my co-workers I will conduct myself according to this agreement at all times.

title: Senior Network Software Engineer (WinSock / PTP)
description:
Job Description

Position: Senior Network Software Engineer (WinSock / PTP)

Level: Senior

Location: Remote

Employment Type: Full-Time/ Part-Time

Working Hours: Palestine Time Zone with partial overlap with U.S. business hours

Contract Duration: 6 Months contract (Extendable based on performance and client needs)

No. of vacancies: 2

Overview:

GGateway is seeking a Senior Network Software Engineer (WinSock / PTP) with strong expertise in low-level Windows networking, including Winsock and NDIS-level development, and Precision Time Protocol (PTP).

The role focuses on designing and building high-performance networking software using the WinSock API on the Windows platform, with strong emphasis on packet-level control, hardware interaction, and time-synchronized communication systems. The ideal candidate will work on performance-critical networking components, including low-latency UDP systems, hardware timestamping, and network timing accuracy.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design, develop, and optimize low-level Windows networking systems using socket programming
  • Build high-performance networking software using Winsock (socket-based development on Windows)
  • Develop production-grade low-level socket programming applications using the WinSock API on the Windows platform
  • Develop and maintain high-throughput UDP/TCP socket-based communication systems
  • Work with NDIS-level networking concepts, including packet flow behavior, offloading, and performance characteristics
  • Implement and support Precision Time Protocol (PTP)-based synchronization solutions
  • Handle low-level socket programming for packet transmission, reception, and control messaging
  • Debug and optimize network traffic at the socket and packet level (latency, jitter, throughput, packet loss)
  • Perform performance tuning for high-load, multi-threaded socket-based systems
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate socket-based networking modules into larger systems
  • Write clean, efficient, production-grade C/C++ socket-based networking code with proper testing and documentation

Required Qualifications

  • Strong hands-on experience in Windows low-level networking (Winsock required)
  • Solid understanding of NDIS and Windows networking architecture
  • Strong proficiency in C / C++ systems programming
  • Experience working with Precision Time Protocol (PTP) synchronization systems and hardware timestamping
  • Deep knowledge of TCP/IP and UDP networking fundamentals
  • Experience building high-performance, multi-threaded networking applications
  • Strong experience in packet-level debugging and network performance optimization
  • Experience in Precision Time Protocol (PTP)
  • Experience working in high-performance or low-latency network environments
  • Strong analytical, debugging, and problem-solving skills in complex system environments

Provide field measurement support for the Gas business by installing, maintaining, calibrating, and troubleshooting equipment used to accurately measure transported natural gas. The position is based in El Paso, Texas, and requires participation in an on-call rotation with a 2-weeks-on/2-weeks-off schedule. The ideal candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to safety, technical expertise, and effective problem-solving in a field environment.

title: Instructional Faculty FT - Biology (Anatomy and Physiology)
description:
Job Description

Montgomery College, Rockville Campus, seeks a full-time Biology faculty member in the Natural Sciences and Engineering (NSE) area to fill a position starting January 2027. This position will primarily teach Human Anatomy and Physiology I and II, with additional teaching responsibilities in introductory biology courses for biology majors and non-majors students. We are seeking an enthusiastic and dedicated educator who exhibits a high degree of professionalism, a strong commitment to our students, and the ability to motivate and educate in an engaging manner. This position is part of a collective bargaining unit.

Anatomy and Physiology I and II serve as a foundational course sequence for students preparing to enter nursing and other health sciences programs at Montgomery College and at other regional institutions. The successful candidate will play a key role in preparing these students for competitive admission and for success in their coursework. All of Montgomery College's science buildings were constructed within the last 15 years and feature state-of-the-art facilities and equipment, including dedicated anatomy and physiology laboratories.

The successful candidate will appreciate teaching in a multi-cultural environment and will welcome the opportunity to work with students with diverse learning abilities. Faculty duties include classroom and laboratory instruction, assessment, curriculum development, advising, professional inquiry, committee work, and instructional technology. The opportunity to engage in research with students is also supported and encouraged.

Teaching assignments may include various delivery modes, such as face-to-face, online, remote, hybrid and/or blended formats during days, evenings, and weekends. Montgomery College has four campuses and instructs courses at area high schools, as part of the growing dual enrollment program. Faculty may be assigned to any of these campuses and/or teaching different modalities.

Duties include but are not limited to:

Teaching and Curriculum

  • Teaches anatomy and physiology and introductory biology courses with a minimum of 30 semester hours per academic year. This teaching position is expected to include Human Anatomy and Physiology I and II (BIOL 212 and BIOL 213), Introductory Biology (BIOL 101 and/or BIOL 150), and other courses in the discipline as needed.

  • Teaches a varied schedule that may include day, evening, early morning, weekend, and accelerated sections. Opportunities may exist for teaching summer classes.

  • Designs, implements, manages, and assesses courses taught in a variety of modes, incorporating the use of a learning management system (Blackboard) and other relevant technology into instruction.

  • Engages students in learning through active, collaborative, and experiential learning approaches, and accommodates students with varying backgrounds and learning styles.

  • Contributes to curriculum development and revision, including course design, and the review and selection of instructional materials.

  • Delivers assigned courses in accordance with College catalog descriptions and the teaching standards of the College and the NSE area.

  • Participates in General Education assessment, course recertification, and program review with the goal of increasing student success.

Laboratory Instruction

  • Designs and prepares laboratory activities for anatomy and physiology courses, collaborating with lab staff on necessary models, specimens, equipment, and instructional supplies.

  • Uses anatomical models, prepared specimens, histological preparations, and instructional technology to support student learning of structure and function.

  • Implements and enforces laboratory safety protocols, including the safe handling and disposal of biological materials and chemicals, in accordance with College policy.

Student Support and Advising

  • Holds regular office hours and maintains availability to students. Mentors and tutors students outside of class to assist them with being successful in college.

  • Advises students about program curricula, health sciences career pathways, and transfer options to four-year institutions.

  • Arranges and promotes scholarship, research, and internship opportunities for students.

  • Advises and supports student clubs and related student activities.

Service and Professional Development

  • Participates in college and community activities that contribute to the growth and development of students, the College, and the community.

  • Serves on and leads department, discipline, campus, and college committees.

  • Stays current in the discipline and pursues continuous professional development, including participation in professional organizations and activities.

Required Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree or higher in a Biological Science or closely related field, with graduate-level preparation in anatomy, physiology, or a related area.

  • One year of demonstrated college-level teaching experience, which may include experience as a graduate teaching assistant or instructor of record.

  • Experience teaching college-level anatomy and physiology.

  • Experience designing and/or setting up hands-on laboratory activities with attention to safety protocols.

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills.

  • Eligible applicants must currently be authorized to work in the United States and not require employer visa sponsorship.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. in a Biological Science or a closely related field.

  • Two or more years of recent college teaching experience.

  • Demonstrated experience teaching a two-semester anatomy and physiology sequence, including both lecture and laboratory.

  • Experience with laboratory methods used in anatomy and physiology instruction, including anatomical models, prepared specimens, anatomical visualization technologies, and/or physiological data acquisition.

  • Experience teaching at a community college, another open-enrollment setting, or otherwise working with students of widely varying academic preparation.

  • Demonstrated experience using varied teaching modalities (face-to-face, blended/hybrid, and online).

  • Demonstrated experience using techniques to engage students in the classroom.

  • Demonstrated commitment to student success including increasing retention, transfer, and graduation.

  • Demonstrated experience in implementing or developing experiential learning opportunities for students.

  • Evidence of ongoing professional development.

Hiring Range: $64,510 - $98,220

Required Application Materials:

Submit a cover letter addressing how your teaching experience, scholarship, professional development, and/or service would contribute to student success in Biology and align with Montgomery College’s mission and vision.

Submit a resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV).

Submit an unofficial copy of your transcripts from the highest degree earned.

Please submit all required materials in a single PDF file with your online application. Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Application Process:

  • Complete online applications must be received by September 18, 2026.

  • Include dates of employment (month/year) in your application or attachment.

  • If selected for an interview, the candidate will be expected to conduct a teaching demonstration.

For degrees earned outside of the U.S., a copy of your education equivalency, conducted by a nationally recognized evaluation service, must be included in your application.

As a condition of employment, the following are required at the time of hire:

  • Successful completion of a background check and degree verification (if applicable).

  • Participation in a retirement plan (Pension or Optional Retirement Plan, depending on the position). If you are already retired from the Maryland State Retirement System, you may not enroll in a Maryland State Retirement System plan at Montgomery College and may have earnings restrictions, per state law.

​

Our benefits package includes: sick leave, paid holidays, medical, dental, vision, group legal benefits, professional development, retirement plan, educational assistance, tuition waiver for employee and dependents, wellness programming including onsite gyms, pools and classes.

If a reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact Human Resources and Strategic Talent Management at 240-567-5353 or HRSTM@montgomerycollege.edu. We require at least two weeks advance notice to enable us to provide the requested accommodation.

title: Lead Engineer
description:
About CORTO

We are CORTO, a cutting-edge software company dedicated to revolutionising the legal industry. Our mission is to empower legal practitioners with AI-driven solutions that streamline their workflow, boost productivity, and provide more efficient client service.

Our team of AI experts and engineers collaborate to develop intelligent software tailored to the unique needs of lawyers, paralegals, and legal assistants. Our innovative AI solutions automate routine tasks, simplify document management, and enhance decision-making, allowing legal professionals to focus on what they do best—providing expert legal counsel.

We’re rapidly scaling from 80 to 250+ employees, with a highly technical workforce where around 75% of the team are developers and engineers. Working alongside our Sydney-based team of passionate high achievers, you’ll join a fast-growing technology business where things rarely stay the same for long - and if you’re smart, caring, and ambitious, you’ll be in great company.

﻿
The Opportunity

We are building a new AI-driven product that will become foundational to our platform, helping lawyers and related professionals get high-quality outcomes safely, with AI seamlessly embedded in their workflow.

There is a clear product vision and a well-defined problem. The build is yours to lead.

What makes it hard, and interesting, is the operating environment. The product holds confidential material for many firms at once, so it has to be safe by construction. Isolation, access control and auditability are not features to be added later, they are the shape of the thing from the first commit.

The first build is deliberately focused, and it will not be the last. It is small enough that one person can hold it in their head and get it genuinely right, and it sets the foundations that the next products in this ecosystem are built on.

Your architecture, your stack

You will choose the languages, frameworks, cloud, data stores and orchestration approach that you believe best meet the product's requirements. It will need to interoperate with our existing platform over a defined integration contract. Beyond that, we care far more about the qualities the system must have than about any particular technology:

  • Reliable, durable handling of long-running work. Nothing lost, and nothing left stale or silent without someone being told;
  • Strong multi-tenant isolation, enforced by design rather than by convention, with opaque tenant identifiers and per-client credentials.
  • Per-person identity and access, scoped to the organisation a person belongs to.
  • A complete, tamper-evident record of who accessed what and what the system did.
  • A security-first posture suited to confidential data and the certifications firms expect, such as ISO 27001 and SOC 2.
  • A deterministic, auditable boundary around what the AI can reach and what it is permitted to act on. The AI proposes, code disposes.
  • Clean seams, so new capabilities and integrations can be added without rebuilding the core.

If you have strong, well-reasoned opinions about how to build systems like this, you will have the autonomy to act on them.

What you’ll do

As the Lead Developer, you will design and build the product end to end, from request handling and AI-driven understanding through to durable task management and high-quality, reliable outputs, and make it foundational to our AI ecosystem. To make that happen you will:

  • Build a new multi-tenant product from zero to one, choosing the stack to fit the requirements.
  • Build scalable, secure, high-performance backend services and a polished admin and supervision experience.
  • Design a safety-first system: untrusted-input handling, a deterministic action boundary, per-tenant isolation and a complete audit trail.
  • Build durable, resumable orchestration for long-running work that delegates to external services.
  • Prototype, test and refine AI-driven features that work reliably with generative AI models and agent- style workflows.
  • Establish engineering processes, DevOps workflows, observability and quality standards.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with other AI teams, product leaders and senior stakeholders.

What you’ll bring

  • You are a curious, self-driven engineer who wants to build meaningful technology.
  • 8+ years of professional experience in full-stack development.
  • Deep experience in system design, distributed systems, database architecture and API design.
  • A track record of making and owning architecture and technology choices, and being accountable for the results.
  • Strong proficiency in at least one modern backend ecosystem and a modern frontend framework, able to work full-stack.
  • Experience building secure, multi-tenant SaaS, ideally with data isolation, encryption and secrets management.
  • Experience designing reliable, long-running or event-driven systems where work must never be lost.
  • Hands-on experience with generative AI, automation workflows or agent-based systems.
  • Familiarity with secure integration patterns and third-party APIs, such as MCP or similar tool and connector approaches.

CORTO is an inclusive, people-first company committed to breaking down institutional barriers that keep people from reaching their potential. If you meet some, but not all the requirements above, we encourage you to still submit your application.

Why join CORTO?

  • Your work matters. We solve real world problems that improve and support local, everyday law firms and related professionals. So they can do their best work for the people in the communities they serve.
  • Make an impact. You won’t be another ‘cog in the wheel’ here. We give full trust and autonomy for you to be heard, to work on big & complex projects – and to make a real difference.
  • Work with a group of authentic, passionate people who love what they do.
  • Well-funded and global. CORTO is part of ATI Global – one of the largest international LegalTech companies.
  • Flexible and hybrid working. We engage, share, and collaborate on ideas and workflows.
  • Career and learning opportunities - we move fast and need smart people to get us where we're going. We are a scaling business and looking for people who want to grow with us.
  • Have fun with us. Celebrations. Socials. Sports teams. Access to sailing and yacht events.
  • We value your well-being with additional time off, gym membership and other perks.
  • Fast-paced tech environment, if we don't disrupt ourselves someone else will do it!
  • Access to LEAP Home - a program unique to the ATI Group to support you in buying your primary residence.

title: Slot Ambassador
description:
At Aquarius Gaming, LLC , we don’t just offer jobs — we build careers. In a business that’s often about flash, we’re the real deal.   • Regularly sit and work at a desk or computer

  • Ability to hear, understand, and distinguish speech and/or other sound in person

title: Associate Director, Responsible AI Solutions
description:
The application deadline is on Friday, October 9, 2026. Please submit both a resume and a cover letter to be considered.

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

The Ford Foundation’s Information Technology team seeks an Associate Director, Responsible AI Solutions. Reporting to the Chief Information and Technology Officer (CITO), the Associate Director leads the development and implementation of ethical, cutting-edge AI solutions that align with our mission. The Associate Director works closely with the CITO and senior leaders across the foundation in refining and implementing the foundation’s evolving AI strategy.

Partnering with staff at all levels and external vendors and consultants, the Associate Director will use their experience, deep systems knowledge and understanding of best practices around governance and policy development to design and scale AI solutions that foster a culture of responsible innovation balancing ethical principles with real world solutions to create significant impact.

HOW YOU WILL CONTRIBUTE

As the Associate Director, Responsible AI Solutions, you will perform the following and/or similar activities:

  • AI Portfolio Management: As the focal point for all AI initiatives within the IT team, manage a dedicated AI portfolio and consult with the cross-functional IT teams on their AI projects, fostering a cohesive approach to AI development and implementation.

  • Develop and implement ethical AI solutions: Identify and translate complex business challenges into AI solutions. This involves assessing organizational needs, recommending ethical solutions, gathering requirements, designing and developing AI solutions, and deploying them into production environments within required budget and quality standards expectations. This includes defining project scope, gaining insight and agreement from others, allocating resources, managing timelines, and mitigating risks.

  • AI Strategy: Collaborate with the CITO and senior leaders from cross-functional teams on refining the foundation’s AI strategy to ensure that the foundation’s AI systems, guidelines, processes, and procedures are aligned to the foundation’s mission and values and are being scaled throughout the entire foundation.

  • Governance & policy development: Monitor evolving AI regulations and data privacy laws. As a key member of the AI Advisory Group, draft, implement, and maintain clear, accessible Responsible AI guidelines, safety policies, and use-case criteria for the whole foundation to follow. Ensures all AI- related activities, all relevant stakeholders are aware of and adhering to ethical guidelines and protecting organizational data. Promote responsible AI development and deployment within the organization across departments, while considering potential biases, fairness, and transparency in AI systems.

  • AI Model evaluation and optimization: Continuously monitor and evaluate the effectiveness and performance of AI models, identifying areas for improvement and implementing optimization strategies to reduce our carbon footprint and enhance accuracy, efficiency, and scalability.

  • Vendor & technology assessment: Remain up-to-date with emerging AI trends, technologies, and best practices. Research and recommend new AI tools and techniques to improve operational efficiency and drive innovation. Evaluate, propose and manage AI vendors and consultants to deliver strategic value within an approved budget.

  • Education, culture & capacity building: Partner with People & Culture and other departments to build organization-wide AI literacy and upskilling, responsible prompt engineering, and ethical awareness. Cultivate a culture of responsible innovation across different teams, empowering non-technical staff to identify potential ethical risks early.

  • Communicate effectively with stakeholders: Clearly and effectively communicate project solutions, requirements and updates, technical details, and AI concepts to technical and non-technical audiences, including senior management, business stakeholders, and team members. Translate complex technical information into clear business value for non-technical stakeholders.

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

  • 8+ years of related professional experience and a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, AI, Machine Learning, or a related field (or an equivalent combination of education and experience).

  • Proficient in Python and AI frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch), with expertise in machine learning, deep learning, NLP, foundational models, and GenAI technologies.

  • Experienced in Generative AI techniques (e.g., LLMs, LangChain, RAG), Agentic architecture, and establishing connections using Model Context Protocol (MCP).

  • Experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Vertex AI, and production deployment using Gemini Enterprise or equivalent platforms (working knowledge of Google’s ADK is a plus).

  • Familiar with major cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), data technologies (SQL, Hadoop, Spark), and AI Ops principles (CI/CD pipelines, containerization, automated testing).

  • Experienced in deploying AI models to cloud environments—optimizing for performance, latency, cost, and resource utilization (GPU/TPU)—and troubleshooting issues like performance drift.

  • Strong capability in working with large datasets, extracting meaningful insights from unstructured data, and understanding content management systems, knowledge graphs, and information retrieval techniques.

  • Demonstrated ability to recommend and apply practical AI solutions to real-world problems within content-rich domains.

  • Deep conceptual understanding of how models process data, exhibit bias, and handle data privacy.

  • Excellent project management skills with experience managing complex AI projects using Agile development methodologies.

  • Experience managing AI vendors and the technical capability to evaluate vendor claims regarding model safety, data retention, and training data provenance.

  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and relationship-management skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts for executive and non-technical audiences.

  • Ways of working and engaging that align with the Foundation’s mission, core values, and commitment to creating a culture of excellence.

This position is primarily a sedentary role. However, the person in this position may need to occasionally move about inside the office to liaise with internal staff, access files, office machinery and a copy machine/printer.

We review global compensation regularly to ensure market competitiveness and equity. The hiring range for this position has been carefully crafted to align with the market.

title: Career Advisor
description:
Career Advisor

As a Career Advisor, you will have the opportunity to make a lasting impact by supporting employees as they explore career pathways, pursue education and training opportunities, and achieve their career goals. We are a nonprofit organization committed to empowering individuals through employment, growth, and opportunity.

The Career Advisor provides individualized coaching, mentoring, and guidance to help employees identify strengths, set goals, and create actionable career plans. This role supports employees with career exploration, resume development, interview preparation, educational planning, tuition assistance programs, and advancement opportunities.

The Career Advisor also builds partnerships with colleges, trade schools, workforce development organizations, and community partners to expand opportunities for employee success. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys traveling throughout Washington State and around the country, building relationships, and helping others reach their full potential.

Location: Bremerton, Washington

Type: Non-Exempt

Compensation: $28.50 - $39.18 per hour (The targeted salary range for this role is between $36.00 - $38.46 per hour.)

Work Schedule: Full-time, Monday – Friday 7:30 am – 4:00 pm (flexible start and end times depending on scheduling needs)

As a Career Advisor, you'll… Career Advisor’s collaborate with Tessera’s functional/operational managers and vocational department to promote career pathways and development for all employees in the Washington State Region of Tessera. These efforts include working with and supporting employees with Employee Career Plans (ECPs) and other career services such as resume writing/updating, interview techniques, creating/updating LinkedIn profiles and job searching.

The Career Advisor utilizes and educates employees about the Tuition Assistance (TA) program at Tessera. This includes the coordinated marketing of the program and sharing of success stories with the Marketing / Communications department. They are responsible for seeking and developing external partnerships with the community to develop workforce development plans and establish and maintain employment pipelines in the Washington State regions of Tessera. This includes working closely with high school transitions programs, colleges, government organizations, and other mission aligned non-profit.

This position travels to sites in Washington State and other locations around the country 6 weeks per year to educate employees about all career services available and reinforce the employee support culture.

  • Provide individualized career guidance, advising, and coaching to employees with the goal of helping employees individually identify their career plans and trajectory.

  • Schedule employee meetings and input ECPS or case-notes about employee interactions in Workday.

  • Work with employees who want access to TA. This includes completing an ECP with all applicants, assisting employees to apply for TA and following up with employees who use TA to obtain all required documents (Receipts, transcripts, etc.). Communicate all TA information with the Career Services Supervisor.

  • Teach and mentor employees through the process of writing resumes, applying for jobs, creating LinkedIn profiles and preparing for interviews.

  • Guide employees through the application process for technical schools, college, or other university programs.

  • Research and explore career paths, certifications, technical trades, college, and university programs.

  • Build and Maintain partnerships with community colleges, trade schools, and universities near our sites in Washington so that you can match our employees with programs that are a good fit.

  • Network with state and federal Workforce Development and career pathways stakeholders.

  • Network with local high schools and youth programs. Work with site leadership to provide job shadows, site tours, and internship opportunities for students interested in the trades.

  • Assist employees with information and applying for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) to alleviate college debts for employees.

  • Work with the tech trades department to create strategies while working with site leadership to “grow our own” particularly within Total Facility Maintenance sites where the average age of our trades workers is over 55.

  • Track labor force trends and data.

  • Work closely with the Workforce Development Team.

  • Have excellent time management, organizational, and written/verbal communication skills.

  • Able to quickly build professional relationships with employees and community partners.

  • Travel to sites in Washington State and other locations around the country 6 weeks per year.

  • All Other Duties as Assigned.

You'd make an excellent Career Advisor if you:

  • Consider yourself a people person.

  • Love working on collaborative teams.

  • Are dedicated to internal and external customer service.

  • Take pride in your work.

  • Are drawn to serving others and want to challenge yourself through mission-driven work.

Tessera is proud to offer a comprehensive compensation and benefits package to our eligible part-time and full-time employees.

Partnership: Works collaboratively with coworkers, supervisors, and stakeholders to achieve shared goals. Integrity: Acts honestly and takes accountability for actions and results.

title: PRN Clinical Laboratory Scientist
description:
Your job is more than a job.

The Clinical Laboratory Scientist performs clinical laboratory testing of blood and body fluid constituents as requested by physicians. Evaluates and reports data for use in diagnosis and treatment of disease. Operates, controls and troubleshoots clinical laboratory equipment.

Your Everyday

Ensures specimens received by the laboratory are acceptable for testing by applying the appropriate criteria. Changes or prepares reagents, controls as necessary and records such in log. Labels, accessions and distributes specimens so that integrity of patient identification is maintained throughout processing. Inoculates specimens from all areas of the body on appropriate media. Initiates orders for blood and/or blood components from the appropriate blood supplier. Follows hospital/laboratory safety and infection control policies and reports variances to section supervisors as they occur.

Operates both primary and secondary instrumentation proficiently. Determines appropriateness of manual methods, micro-methods, back-up procedures and initiates such procedures. Through use of the computer system, compares patient results to previous results during the same encounter and investigates discrepancies. Reports test results within established departmental turn-around times after verifying documentation is complete and accurate.

Prepares and interprets gram stains and other wet and dry preparations for bacteriology and parasitology. Performs all routine procedures including, but not limited to, ABORH typing and retesting, antibody detection and identification, compatibility testing and serology procedures. Prepares blood components while maintaining aseptic technique and proper storage. Evaluates serological reactivity to assist with antibody identification and crossmatch incompatibilities. Follows universal precautions at all times when dealing with blood or body fluids. Disinfects counter tops at the end of the shift with appropriate cleaner.


Operates, calibrates, conducts performance checks and maintains any clinical laboratory instrument or equipment after orientation. Troubleshoots basic instrument malfunctions and documents in the appropriate action log. Determines when an instrument’s service representative should be contacted for assistance. Analyzes quality control material for each procedure, records values according to section policy and reports to technical Supervisor when results are outside established limits. Performs comparison studies of precision, accuracy and linearity on new or existing procedures and reports results by established deadlines. Performs and accurately records proficiency surveys, properly routes form and copies within the specified time frame. Performs all aspects of reagent quality control as specified in the quality control manuals. Assists in the clinical orientation of new or less skilled laboratory personnel as requested by the section Supervisor. Assures proper packaging and disposal of waste chemicals. Maintains proper documentation (log) of generated waste.


Performs order or result entry (manual or computerized) and reviews information for accuracy before verification. Documents Critical Call Value notification, duplicate checking, date and time of performance, technologist initials and expected age related “normal” values on all down-time reports as appropriate.


Checks instruments and benches assigned for appropriate reagent and supply levels and replenishes when necessary. Notifies appropriate person of low inventory items or of any out-of-date reagents contaminated or otherwise unacceptable. Records receipt of supplies and reagents, properly initialing and dating the inventory items at receipt, time put into use and expiration. Ensures adequate inventory levels are available for incoming shifts.

Receives tissue specimens from surgery, autopsy and the nursing floors. Performs proper processing and preservation of tissue specimens. Complies with proper specimen storage and preservation of all other non-tissue specimens for non-core laboratory. Prepares necessary reagents and collection supplies for assisting with bone marrow aspirations according to physician orders. Assists physicians in the procurement of bone marrow specimens in accordance with departmental and Hospital policies. Performs special stains and follows protocols as appropriate.

The Must-Haves

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Clinical Lab Generalist licensed by Louisiana State Board of Medical Examiners as CLG or CLS

title: Field Supervisor, Pool Renovtion
description:
Join the Experts in Pool Surfacing and Renovation

At Jackson Pool Surfaces, we believe pool surfacing is more than a job - it's a craft. Based in Grandview, Missouri, we specialize in delivering high-quality pool resurfacing and renovation services, providing an outstanding customer experience from the initial call to the final walkthrough.


We are seeking a dependable team member who ensures high-quality work, leads others effectively, and delivers all tasks and projects on time with a strong focus on exceptional client satisfaction.


Role Summary:

The Field Service, Pool Renovation position serves as a central point of coordination for active pool renovation projects and day-to-day field operations. This position provides on-site leadership, coordinates crews across multiple job sites, and ensures projects remain aligned with operational expectations, project requirements, and company quality standards.


Managing several projects and priorities at once, this role monitors progress in the field and takes action to address issues as they arise. The role is responsible for helping keep projects on schedule while ensuring all work is performed safely, efficiently, and according to established specifications.


Success in the Field Service, Pool Renovation position requires hands-on swimming pool construction and renovation knowledge, strong attention to detail, and the ability to effectively coordinate field crews and respond to changing project needs. This role plays an essential role in maintaining consistency, quality, and productivity across renovation sites.


Reporting Relationship: Owner


Classification: Full-time, Exempt


Schedule: This is a full-time, field-based position with a schedule that varies based on project demands and seasonal workload. Workdays typically begin early in the morning, and hours may extend later in the day during peak seasons to ensure project completion. This role is performed primarily on active job sites rather than in an office setting.


Scope of Role:

  • Manage multiple concurrent pool renovation projects, coordinating crews, schedules, and resources to ensure timely, high-quality project completion
  • Lead crews and provide clear direction on work execution, productivity, and quality standards
  • Monitor project timelines and adjust as needed to keep work on schedule
  • Lead field quality assurance by conducting inspections throughout each phase of construction to ensure work meets company quality standards and project specifications
  • Identify deficiencies, implement corrective actions, and hold team members accountable for consistent workmanship and quality through project completion
  • Coordinate with internal teams to ensure job sites are prepared with the materials, equipment, and labor needed for efficient execution
  • Train, coach, and provide real-time feedback to team members on proper techniques, safety practices, and company expectations
  • Communicate project progress, risks, and updates to leadership
  • Ensure job sites are maintained in a clean, organized, and safe condition in accordance with company standards and safety requirements
  • Ensure proper use and care of materials, tools, and equipment
  • Support final walkthroughs and ensure projects are completed to standard
  • Collect field measurements, photographs, site conditions, and project specifications to support accurate estimating, quoting, and scope development for renovation projects and add-on work
  • Monitor labor, materials, and crew performance to support efficient project delivery, cost control, profitability, and reduction of waste or rework


Required Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of experience in construction, renovation, or a related trade; relevant pool experience is required
  • Previous experience in a leadership or supervisory role
  • Solid understanding of job sequencing and construction quality standards
  • Strong problem-solving skills in a field-based environment
  • Clear communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with both field crews and office staff
  • Proficient with workplace technology, including CRM systems, Microsoft Teams, Outlook, and other mobile and office applications, with the ability to use technology effectively to communicate, manage projects, and complete daily job responsibilities
  • Valid driver's license and ability to travel between job sites
  • Bilingual in English and Spanish required


Work Conditions:

Work is primarily performed on active construction job sites and requires frequent travel between locations to oversee project operations, inspect work, and support field activities.


The position requires prolonged standing and walking, frequent movement throughout active job sites, and the ability to bend, kneel, reach, and occasionally lift, carry, push, pull, or turn while handling materials, tools, or equipment as needed. Work is performed outdoors in all weather conditions, including heat, cold, rain, humidity, and varying terrain. The role requires the ability to safely navigate active construction environments, communicate effectively in person and by email, text, and phone, and occasionally lift or move materials weighing up to approximately 100 pounds.

Compensation: $70,000–$90,000 annually, based on experience and qualifications, with the upper end of the range reflecting candidates with relevant pool industry experience and bilingual proficiency (English/Spanish).


Benefits:

  • Health insurance stipend
  • Employer-matched retirement plan
  • Paid time off and paid holidays
  • Long-term growth opportunity within a rapidly growing company


Jackson Pool Surfaces is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to considering all qualified applicants. If you meet the qualifications and are excited about this opportunity, we would welcome the opportunity to review your resume. Please note that we do not provide visa sponsorship at this time and do not engage outside agencies or recruiters for any roles.
